12:1: As for the discussion of the disconnected letters, it was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. And His statement: These are the verses of the Book means these are the verses of the Book, which is the clear Qur'an, meaning the clear and evident that explains the ambiguous things, interprets them and clarifies them. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand. This is because the Arabic language is the most eloquent, clearest, most comprehensive and most capable of conveying the meanings that exist in the souls. For this reason, the most honorable of books was sent down in the most honorable of languages, to the most honorable of messengers through the embassy of the most honorable of angels. This was in the most honorable of places on earth, and its revelation began in the most honorable of months of the year, which is Ramadan, so it was perfected in every way. For this reason, the Most High said: We relate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an because of Our revelation of this Qur'an to you. The reason for the revelation of this verse was narrated by Ibn Jarir: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, Hakam Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, why don’t you tell us a story? So the verse was revealed: We relate to you the best of stories, and he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Amr bin Qais, without a chain of transmission. He also said: Muhammad bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, Amr bin Muhammad told us, Khalid Al-Saffar informed us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, on the authority of his father, who said: The Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: He recited it to them for a while, and they said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you tell us a story? Then God the Almighty revealed, “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book” until His saying, That you may understand. Then he recited it to them for a while, and they said: O Messenger of God, if you would tell us, then God the Almighty revealed, God has sent down the best statement the verse, and mentioned the hadith. Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq bin Rahawayh on the authority of Amr bin Muhammad Al-Qurashi Al-Manqari with it, and Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were tired of one religion and said: O Messenger of God, tell us, so God revealed, God has sent down the best statement. Then they were tired of another religion and said: O Messenger of God, tell us above the hadith and below the Qur’an, meaning stories, so God the Almighty revealed, “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an that you may understand. We narrate to you the best stories” the verse, and they wanted the hadith, so he guided them to the best hadith, and they wanted the stories, so he guided them to the best stories. What is appropriate to mention in relation to this noble verse that includes praise for the Qur’an, and that it is sufficient for all other books is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Surayj bin Al-Nu’man narrated to us, Hisham informed us, Mujalid informed us on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that Umar bin Al-Khattab came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a book that he had obtained from some of the People of the Book, and he read it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: He became angry and said: “Are you fooling around with it, O son of Al-Khattab? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I have brought it to you pure and white. Do not ask them about anything lest they tell you the truth and you deny it, or falsehood and you believe it. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if Moses were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me.” Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Thabit, who said: Umar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I passed by a brother of mine from Qurayzah, and he wrote for me comprehensive verses from the Torah. Should I not show them to you? He said: The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, changed. Abdullah bin Thabit said: I said to him: Do you not see what is on the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Umar said: We are pleased with God as our Lord, Islam as our religion, and Muhammad as our Messenger. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was relieved and he said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if Moses were to appear among you and you were to follow him and abandon me, you would go astray. You are my portion among the nations, and I am your portion among the prophets.” Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Abdul Ghaffar bin Abdullah bin al-Zubayr told us, Ali bin Musa’ar told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Khalifa bin Qais, on the authority of Khalid bin Urfata, who said: I was sitting with Umar when a man from Abd al-Qais, whose home was in Sous, was brought to him. Umar said to him: Are you so-and-so bin so-and-so al-Abdi? He said: Yes. He said: Are you the one who lives in Sous? He said: Yes. So he hit him with a stick he had with him. The man said: What is wrong with me, O Commander of the Faithful? Umar said to him: Sit down. So he sat down and recited to him: “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an that you might understand. We narrate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur’an, although before it you were among the unaware.” So he recited it to him three times and hit him three times. The man said to him: What is wrong with me, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: You are the one who abrogated the Book of Daniel. He said: Order me what you command me to do, and I will follow it. He said: “Go and erase it with hot water and white wool, then do not read it or teach it to anyone. If I hear that you have read it or taught it to anyone, I will punish you.” Then he said to him: Sit down. So he sat in front of him and said: “I went and copied a book from the People of the Book, then I brought it on a leather cover. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “What is this in your hand, O Umar?” I said: O Messenger of God, a book that I copied so that we may increase our knowledge with it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry until his cheeks turned red. Then the call to prayer was made, and the Ansar said: “Has your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, become angry?” The weapon, the weapon, so they came until they surrounded the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “O people, I have been given the most comprehensive and conclusive words, and they have been shortened for me, and I have brought them to you pure and white, so do not act rashly and do not be deceived by the rash.” Omar said: So I stood up and said: I am satisfied with God as Lord, Islam as religion, and you as Messenger, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his interpretation, shortened, from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, and this is a strange hadith from this aspect, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is Abu Shaybah al-Wasiti, and they weakened him and his sheikh. Al-Bukhari said: His hadith is not authentic. I said: A witness narrated from him from another source. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Ismaili said: Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told me, Yaqub bin Sufyan told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Al-Ala Al-Zubaidi told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, Abdullah bin Salem Al-Ash'ari told us on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, Salim bin Aamer told us that Jubayr bin Nufayr told them that two men were in Homs during the caliphate of Umar, may God be pleased with him, so he sent to them among those he sent from the people of Homs. They had written down a large quantity of Salasafa from the Jews, so they took it with them to consult the Commander of the Faithful about it, saying: If the Commander of the Faithful approves it for us, we will increase our desire for it, and if he forbids us from it, we will reject it. So when they came to him, they said: We are in the land of the People of the Book, and we hear from them words that make our skin crawl, so should we take some of it or leave it? He said: Perhaps you have written some of it? They said: No. He said: I will tell you: I set out during the lifetime of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until I came to Khaybar, and I found a Jew saying something that I liked. I said: Will you write down what you say? He said: Yes. So I brought a leather cover and he began to dictate to me until I wrote on the hump. When I returned, I said: O Prophet of God, and I told him. He said: Bring it to me. So I set out, desiring something, hoping that I might have brought the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) something that he liked. When I brought it, he said: Sit down and read to me. So I read for a while, then I looked at the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it was changing colors. I was confused by the difference, and I could not make out a single letter of it. When he saw what was wrong with me, he lifted it up and began to trace it, one by one, erasing it with his saliva, and he was saying: Do not follow these people, for they have strayed and become straying, until he erased the last letter, one by one. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: If I had known that you had written anything of it, I would have made you an example for this nation. They said: By God, we will never write anything of it. So they went out with their swords and dug a hole for it. They did not spare any effort to dig it deep and buried it. That was the last time they saw it. And thus Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Yazid Al-Ju’fi on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abdullah bin Thabit Al-Ansari on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab in a similar manner. And Abu Dawud narrated in Al-Marasil from the hadith of Abu Qilabah on the authority of Omar in a similar manner. And God knows best.

They had written down a large quantity of Salasafa from the Jews, so they took it with them to consult the Commander of the Faithful about it, saying: If the Commander of the Faithful approves it for us, we will increase our desire for it, and if he forbids us from it, we will reject it. So when they came to him, they said: We are in the land of the People of the Book, and we hear from them words that make our skin crawl, so should we take some of it or leave it? He said: Perhaps you have written some of it? They said: No. He said: I will tell you: I set out during the lifetime of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until I came to Khaybar, and I found a Jew saying something that I liked. I said: Will you write down what you say? He said: Yes. So I brought a leather cover and he began to dictate to me until I wrote on the hump. When I returned, I said: O Prophet of God, and I told him. He said: Bring it to me. So I set out, desiring something, hoping that I might have brought the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) something that he liked. When I brought it, he said: Sit down and read to me. So I read for a while, then I looked at the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it was changing colors. I was confused by the difference, and I could not make out a single letter of it. When he saw what was wrong with me, he lifted it up and began to trace it, one by one, erasing it with his saliva, and he was saying: Do not follow these people, for they have strayed and become straying, until he erased the last letter, one by one. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: If I had known that you had written anything of it, I would have made you an example for this nation. They said: By God, we will never write anything of it. So they went out with their swords and dug a hole for it. They did not spare any effort to dig it deep and buried it. That was the last time they saw it. And thus Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Yazid Al-Ju’fi on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abdullah bin Thabit Al-Ansari on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab in a similar manner. And Abu Dawud narrated in Al-Marasil from the hadith of Abu Qilabah on the authority of Omar in a similar manner. And God knows best.
12:4: God the Almighty says: Mention to your people, O Muhammad, in your stories to them, the story of Joseph when he said to his father, and his father was Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, peace be upon them, as Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Samad told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Omar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The generous one, the son of the generous one, the son of the generous one, is Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, and he narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abdul Samad, and Al-Bukhari also said: Muhammad told us, Abdah informed us, on the authority of Ubaidullah, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, Which people are the most generous? He said, The most generous of them in the sight of God is the most pious. They said, We are not asking you about this. He said, The most generous of people is Joseph, the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Friend of God. They said, We are not asking you about this. He said, Then do you ask me about the origins of the Arabs? They said, Yes. He said, The best of you in the pre-Islamic era are the best of you in Islam if they understand. Then he said: Abu Usamah followed him on the authority of Ubayd God. Ibn Abbas said: The vision of the prophets is a revelation. The interpreters have spoken about the interpretation of this dream, that the eleven stars are his brothers, and they were eleven men other than him, and the sun and the moon are his mother and father. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. Its interpretation occurred after forty years, and it was said: eighty years, when he raised his parents to the throne, which was his bed, and his brothers were in front of him. “And they fell down before him in prostration. And he said: O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true.” It was mentioned in the hadith about naming these eleven stars. Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Sa`id Al-Kindi told me, Al-Hakam ibn Dhahir told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, on the authority of Jabir, who said: A Jewish man called Bustanah the Jew came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: O Muhammad, tell me about the stars that Joseph saw prostrating to him. What are their names? He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent for a while and did not answer him with anything. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to him and told him their names. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for him and said: Will you be a believer if I tell you their names? He said: Yes. He said: Jiryan, Al-Tariq, Al-Dhiyal, Dhu Al-Kanafat, Qabis, Wathab, Amudan, Al-Failaq, Al-Misbah, Al-Duruh, Dhu Al-Fargh, Al-Dhiya, and Al-Nour. The Jew said: Yes, by God, they are their names. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Al-Dala'il from the hadith of Saeed bin Mansour from Al-Hakam bin Dhahir. This hadith was narrated by the two hadith masters Abu Ya'la Al-Mawsili and Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar in their Musnads, and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir. As for Abu Ya'la, he narrated it from four of his sheikhs from Al-Hakam bin Dhahir with it, and he added: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When Joseph saw it, he told it to his father Jacob, and his father said to him: This is a scattered matter that God will gather later. - He said - And the sun is his father and the moon is his mother.” Al-Hakam bin Dhahir Al-Fazari is the only one to narrate it, and the imams declared him weak and most of them abandoned him. Al-Jawzjani said: He is weak, and he is a good hadith master. Then he mentioned the hadith narrated from Jabir that a Jew asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the stars that Joseph saw, what were their names? And that he answered him. Then he said: Al-Hakam bin Dhahir is the only one to narrate it, and the four declared it weak.
12:5: God Almighty says, informing about what Jacob said to his son Joseph when he told him what he saw of this vision, the interpretation of which was the submission of his brothers to him, and their excessive glorification of him to the point that they prostrated to him in reverence, respect and honor. Jacob, peace be upon him, feared that he would tell this dream to one of his brothers, lest they envy him for it and seek to harm him out of envy of him. For this reason, he said to him: Do not tell your brothers about your vision, lest they plot against you, meaning they plot against you in a way that would harm you. For this reason, the Sunnah was confirmed from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If one of you sees something he likes, let him tell it, and if he sees something he dislikes, let him turn to his other side, let him spit to his left three times, let him seek refuge with God from its evil, and let him not tell it to anyone, for it will not harm him.” In another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and some of the people of Sunnah from the narration of Muawiyah bin Haidah, Al-Qushayri, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And Sallam said: The vision of a flying man is like a bird unless it is interpreted, and if it is interpreted, it will come true. From this we can understand the command to conceal a blessing until it exists and becomes apparent, as mentioned in the hadith: Seek help in fulfilling needs by concealing them, for every person with a blessing is envied.
12:6: God Almighty says, informing about what Jacob said to his son Joseph: Just as your Lord chose you and showed you these stars with the sun and the moon prostrating to you, “so will your Lord choose you meaning He chooses you and selects you for His prophethood, and will teach you the interpretation of dreams Mujahid and more than one said: meaning the interpretation of dreams, and will complete His favor upon you meaning by sending you and inspiring you, and for this reason He said: just as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham meaning the friend, and Isaac his son who was the sacrificed one saying, but it is not the most likely, indeed your Lord is Knowing and Wise meaning He knows best where to place His message, as He said in the other verse.
12:7: God Almighty says: There were indeed signs in the story of Joseph and his experience with his brothers, meaning a lesson and sermons for those who asked about that and inquired about it, for it is an amazing story that deserves to be told about it. When they said, ‘Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we,’ meaning they swore, by God, that Joseph and his brother, meaning Benjamin, who was his brother on his mother’s side, are dearer to our father than we, and we are a clan, meaning a group, so how could he have loved those two more than the group? Indeed, our father is in manifest error, meaning in his preference for them over us, and his love for them more than us. Know that there is no evidence of the prophethood of Joseph’s brothers, and the apparent meaning of this context indicates otherwise. Some people claim that revelation was sent to them after that, and this is questionable, and the one who claims this needs evidence. They only mentioned the words of God Almighty: Say, ‘We believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes.’ This is likely because the clans of the Children of Israel are called tribes, just as the Arabs are called tribes and the non-Arabs are called peoples. God Almighty mentions that He sent revelation to the prophets from the tribes of the Children of Israel, so He mentioned them in general because they are many, but each tribe is from the lineage of a man from Joseph’s brothers. There is no evidence that these individuals were sent to, and God knows best. Kill Joseph or cast him out to some land, so that your father’s favor will be yours alone. They say: This one who competes with you in your father’s love for you, eliminate him from your father’s face, so that he will be yours alone, either by killing him or casting him out to some land where you can rest from him, and you can be yours with your father and you will be after him. “A righteous people” so they intended repentance before committing the sin One of them said Qatada and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And the eldest of them was named Reuben. Al-Suddi said: The one who said that was Judah. Mujahid said: He is Simon Peter Do not kill Joseph meaning do not reach the point of killing him in your enmity and hatred towards him, and they had no way to kill him because God Almighty wanted something from him that must be carried out and completed by inspiring him with prophethood, and by empowering him in the land of Egypt and ruling it, so God turned them away from him by Reuben’s words about him and his suggestion to them to throw him into the bottom of the well which is at its bottom. Qatada said: It is the well of Jerusalem Some of the travelers will pick him up meaning the passing travelers, so you will rest from him with this and there is no need to kill him if you are going to do meaning if you are determined to do what you say. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: They agreed on a great matter of severing family ties, disobeying parents, and showing little compassion to the innocent young child, and to the perishing old child who has rights, sanctity, and virtue, and his danger to God, along with the right of the father over his son, in order to separate him from his father and beloved despite his advanced age and the frailty of his bones, despite his position with God among those who loved him as a young child, and from his son despite his weak strength, young age, and need for his father’s kindness and peace with him. May God forgive them, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. They have undertaken a great matter. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Salamah bin al-Fadl on his authority.

12:11: When they conspired to take him and throw him in the well as their elder brother Reuben had suggested to them, they came to their father Jacob, peace be upon him, and said: What is the matter with you? Do not trust us with Joseph, and indeed, we are his sincere advisors. This is an introduction and a claim, and they wanted something else because of the envy in their hearts for his father’s love for him. Send him with us. That is, send him with us. Tomorrow he will graze and play. Some of them read with a ya’. He will graze and play. Ibn Abbas said: He will strive and be active. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and others said the same. And indeed, we will guard him. They said: We will guard him and protect him for your sake.
12:12: When they conspired to take him and throw him in the well as their elder brother Reuben had suggested to them, they came to their father Jacob, peace be upon him, and said: What is the matter with you? Do not trust us with Joseph, and indeed, we are his sincere advisors. And indeed, we will guard him. They said: We will guard him and protect him for your sake.
12:13: God the Almighty says, informing about His Prophet Jacob that he said to his sons in response to their request to send Joseph with them to pasture in the desert, Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, meaning that it is difficult for me to be separated from him for the duration of your taking him with you until he returns, and that is due to his intense love for him because of what he sees in him of great goodness and the characteristics of prophethood and perfection in character and morals, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him. And His statement, And I fear that a wolf will eat him while you are heedless of him, means: And I fear that you will be busy with your throwing and pasturing him, and a wolf will come and eat him while you are unaware. So they took this word from his mouth, and made it their excuse for what they did, and they said, answering him about it at the present moment, If the wolf eats him while we are a group, then we will surely be losers, meaning: If the wolf attacks him and eats him from among us while we are a group, then we will surely perish and helpless.
12:14: God the Almighty says, informing about His Prophet Jacob that he said to his sons in response to their request to send Joseph with them to pasture in the desert, Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, meaning that it is difficult for me to be separated from him for the duration of your taking him with you until he returns, and that is due to his intense love for him because of what he sees in him of great goodness and the characteristics of prophethood and perfection in character and morals, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him. 12:15: God Almighty says: When his brothers took him from his father after consulting him about that, they agreed to put him in the bottom of the well. This is an exaggeration of what they did, that they all agreed to throw him in the bottom of that well, and they had taken him from his father, in what they showed him as an honor to him, and to expand and broaden his chest, and to bring him joy. It is said that when Jacob, peace be upon him, sent him with them, he embraced him, kissed him, and prayed for him. Al-Suddi and others mentioned that there was nothing between their honoring him and showing him harm except that they disappeared from his father’s sight and hid from him. Then they began to harm him with words, cursing, and the like, and actions, such as hitting, and the like. Then they brought him to that well in which they had agreed to throw him. They tied him with a rope and lowered him into it. When he sought refuge with one of them, he would slap him and curse him, and when he clung to the edges of the well, they would hit his hands, then they cut the rope halfway, so he fell into the water. He drowned him, then climbed to a rock in the middle of it called Al-Raghufah, and stood on it. And His statement: And We inspired him, ‘You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they perceive not.’ God Almighty says, mentioning His kindness, mercy, reward, and sending down ease in times of hardship: He inspired Joseph in that difficult situation to comfort his heart and strengthen him, “Do not grieve over what you are in, for there is relief and a good way out for you from that, and God will give you victory over them and raise you and elevate your status, and you will inform them of what they did to you of this deed.” And His statement: And they perceive not. Mujahid and Qatadah said: And they perceive not refers to God’s inspiration to him. Ibn Abbas said: You will inform them of what they did to you, and they do not know you or sense you, as Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Sadaqah bin Ubadah Al-Asadi told us on the authority of his father, I heard Ibn Abbas say: When Joseph’s brothers entered upon him and he recognized them but they did not recognize him, he said: The measure was brought and he placed it on his hand, then he tapped it and understood, then he said: This cup informs me that you had a brother from your father called Joseph, who brought him close to you, and that you took him and threw him into the bottom of the well, he said: Then he tapped it and understood, he said: So you came to your father and said: The wolf ate him and you brought false blood on his shirt, he said: So some of them said to each other: This cup informs him of your report. Ibn Abbas said: We do not think that this verse was revealed except about them: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive.
12:16: God Almighty says, informing us about what Joseph's brothers did after they threw him into the bottom of the well, then they returned to their father in the darkness of the night, crying and showing sorrow and grief for Joseph and grieving for their father, and they said, apologizing for what happened, as they claimed, Indeed, we went racing meaning to throw ourselves into the air, and we left Joseph with our belongings meaning our clothes and belongings, and the wolf ate him, which was the one who had been afraid of him and warned about him. And His saying: And you would not believe us, even if we were truthful, is a great kindness in confirming what they are trying to do. They say: We know that you will not believe us in this case, even if we were truthful to you, so how is it that you accuse us of that, because you feared that the wolf would eat him, so the wolf ate him, so you are excused for your denial of us because of the strangeness of what happened, and the amazing thing that happened to us in this matter of ours. And they brought his shirt with false blood, meaning a lie and fabrication. This is one of the actions with which they confirm the plot they conspired to commit, which is that they took a young goat, as mentioned by Mujahid, As-Suddi and others, so they slaughtered it and smeared Joseph’s garment with its blood, imagining that this was his shirt that the wolf had eaten, and some of its blood had gotten into it, but they forgot to tear it. For this reason, this action was not expected of the Prophet of God, Jacob, but rather he said to them, turning away from their words to what had occurred in his soul of their confusion with him, Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so have patience. Meaning, I will be patient. Be patient with this matter that you have agreed upon until God makes it easy with His help and kindness. And God is the one sought for help against what you describe, meaning against what you mention of lies and impossibilities. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they brought his shirt with false blood. He said: If a wild animal had eaten it, it would have torn the shirt. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said. Mujahid said: Patience is beautiful in which there is no impatience. Hisham narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yahya, on the authority of Hubban bin Abi Jabalah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about his statement: So be patient in a beautiful way. He said: Patience in which there is no complaint. This is a mursal. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Al-Thawri said, on the authority of some of his companions, that he said: Three things are from patience: that you do not speak of your pain, or your calamity, and that you do not praise yourself. Al-Bukhari mentioned here the hadith of Aisha regarding the slander until he mentioned her statement: By God, I do not find an example for me and you except as Abu Yusuf said: So be patient in a beautiful way, and God is the one sought for help against that which you describe.
12:17: God Almighty says, informing us about what Joseph's brothers did after they threw him into the bottom of the well, then they returned to their father in the darkness of the night, crying and showing sorrow and grief for Joseph and grieving for their father, and they said, apologizing for what happened, as they claimed, "Indeed, we went racing meaning to throw ourselves into the air, and we left Joseph with our belongings meaning our clothes and belongings, and the wolf ate him", which was the one who had been afraid of him and warned about him. And His saying: And you would not believe us, even if we were truthful, is a great kindness in confirming what they are trying to do. They say: We know that you will not believe us in this case, even if we were truthful to you, so how is it that you accuse us of that, because you feared that the wolf would eat him, so the wolf ate him, so you are excused for your denial of us because of the strangeness of what happened, and the amazing thing that happened to us in this matter of ours. And they brought his shirt with false blood, meaning a lie and fabrication. This is one of the actions with which they confirm the plot they conspired to commit, which is that they took a young goat, as mentioned by Mujahid, As-Suddi and others, so they slaughtered it and smeared Joseph’s garment with its blood, imagining that this was his shirt that the wolf had eaten, and some of its blood had gotten into it, but they forgot to tear it. All these ten verses were revealed concerning Aisha, the mother of the believers, may God be pleased with her, when the people of slander and calumny among the hypocrites accused her of what they said of pure lies and slander, for which God Almighty was jealous and for his Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. So God Almighty revealed her innocence to protect the honor of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and God Almighty said: Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you, meaning a group among you, meaning it was not one or two, but a group. The foremost in this curse was Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, the head of the hypocrites, for he used to gather it and embellish it, until it entered the minds of some of the Muslims and they spoke of it, and others among them permitted it, and the matter remained like this for about a month until the Qur’an was revealed, and the context of that is in the authentic hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Alqama ibn Waqqas, and Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud told me about the hadith of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the people of slander said to her what they said, and God Almighty exonerated her. All of them told me a portion of her hadith, and some of them were more knowledgeable of her hadith than others and more reliable in their narration. I have memorized from each one of them the hadith that he told me on the authority of Aisha, and some of their hadiths confirm each other. They mentioned that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to go on a journey, he would cast lots among his wives, and whichever of them won, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out with her. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: So he drew lots among us during a campaign he participated in, and my lot won, and I went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was after the veil was revealed. I would be carried in my litter and dismounted in it, during our journey until…” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his expedition and returned and we approached Medina. One night he gave the call to depart, so I got up when he gave the call to depart and walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my business, I went to my saddlebag and felt my chest. I saw that a necklace of Dhofar agate had broken. I went back and looked for my necklace, but my search for it delayed me. The group who were transporting me came and carried my litter and loaded it onto the camel I was riding, thinking that I was in it. She said: At that time, women were light, not heavy and not covered with meat. They only ate a small amount of food, so the people did not find the lightness of the litter strange when they lifted it and carried it. I was a young girl, so they sent the camel and set out, and I found my necklace after the army had continued. I came to their homes and there was no one calling or answering. I headed towards the house I was in, and I thought that the people would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my house, my eyes overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan Ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had gone out from behind the army. He set out early in the morning and was at my house. He saw the blackness of a sleeping person, so he came to me and recognized me when he saw me. He had seen me before the veil, so I woke up with his plea for mercy when he recognized me. I covered my face with my cloak, and by God, he did not say a word to me nor did I hear a word from him except his plea for mercy until he made his mount kneel. He stepped on its hand and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had dismounted in the middle of the afternoon. Those who perished were killed because of me, and the one who bore the brunt of it was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We arrived in Madinah and I was ill when we arrived for a month while the people were pouring out the words of the slanderers, but I did not feel any of that. What makes me suspicious in my pain is that I do not see from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the kindness that I see from him when I am ill. Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, enters and greets, then says, How are you? That is what made me suspicious and I did not feel any evil until I went out after I had recovered, and Umm Masrah went out with me before the places where we defecate, and we do not go out except from night to night, and that was before we took shelter near our houses and we were ordered, as was the first order of the Arabs in taking a walk in the wilderness, and we were bothered by shelters that we take them in our houses, so I set out with Umm Masrah, who is the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf, and her mother is the daughter of Sakhr ibn Amir, the aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son is Masrah ibn Athatah ibn Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. I and the daughter of Abu Ruhm, Umm Masrah, came back to my house when we had finished our business, and Umm Masrah stumbled in her cloak, and she said: May Masrah be cursed! I said to her: What a bad thing you have said, cursing a man who witnessed Badr! She said: Oh, you are a fool, did you not hear what he said? I said: What did he say? She said: She told me what the slanderers had said, so my illness increased to my illness, and when I returned to my house, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came in to me and greeted me, then he said: How are you? So I said to him: Will you give me permission to go to my parents? She said: And at that time I wanted to confirm the report from them, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave me permission. So I went to my parents and said to my mother: O my mother, what are the people talking about? She said: O my daughter, take it easy, for by God, there has rarely been a beautiful woman with a man who loves her and who has co-wives except that they talk about her a lot. She said: I said: Glory be to God, are the people talking about her? So I cried that night until morning, and my tears could not stop and I could not sleep. Then I woke up crying again. She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, and sought their advice about separating from his wife. She said: As for Usamah ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on what he knew of the innocence of his wife and on what he knew in himself of love for them. Usamah said: O Messenger of God, they are your family and we know nothing but good about them. As for Ali ibn Abi Talib, he said: O Messenger of God, God has not made things difficult for you, and there are many women other than her. If you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth. She said: So the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, called Barrah and said: O Barrah, did you see anything suspicious in Aisha? Barrah said to him: By the One Who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything from her that I would be more suspicious of than a young slave girl who sleeps while her family is cooking dough, then the goats come and eat it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up that day and apologized to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was on the pulpit: O group of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man who has harmed my family? By God, I have never known anything about my family except good. They have mentioned a man about whom I have never known anything except good, and he never entered upon my family except with me. Sa`d bin Mu`adh Al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said: I excuse you from him, O Messenger of God. If he is from the Aws, we will strike his neck, and if he is from our brothers from the Khazraj, you will order us to do as you command. She said: Sa`d bin `Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj and a righteous man, stood up, but his zeal carried him and said to Sa`d bin Mu`adh: By God, you will not kill him, nor will you be able to kill him. Asid bin Hudayr, the cousin of Sa`d bin Mu`adh, stood up and said to Sa`d bin `Ubadah: You have lied! By God, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of the hypocrites. So the two tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj, clashed. Until they were about to fight while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was standing on the pulpit, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept calming them down until they were silent and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was silent. She said: And I wept that day, my tears not stopping nor could I sleep, and my parents thought that crying was going to split my liver. She said: While they were sitting with me and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to see me, so I gave her permission and she sat and wept with me. While we were like that, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon us and greeted us and then sat down. She said: He has not sat with me since what was said was said, and he remained for a month without receiving any revelation about me. She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) bore witness when he sat down, then he said: As for what follows, O Aisha, such and such has reached me about you. If you are innocent, God will acquit you, and if you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness from God and then repent to Him, for when a servant confesses to a sin and then repents, God will repent to him. She said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished speaking, my tears stopped. Until I did not feel a drop of it, so I said to my father: Answer the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on my behalf. He said: By God, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I said to my mother: Answer the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on my behalf. She said: By God, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: I said, and I am a young girl who did not memorize much of the Qur’an. By God, I know that you have heard this hadith until it settled in your souls and you believed in it. If I tell you that I am innocent, and God knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me in that. And if I confess something, and God knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By God, I do not find an example for me and you except as Abu Yusuf said: So be patient, and God is the sought for help against that which you describe. She said: Then I turned and lay down on my bed. She said: And by God, at that time I knew that I was innocent and that God, the Most High, would acquit me because of my innocence. But by God, I did not think that a revelation would be revealed concerning me that would be recited, and my affair was too insignificant in my soul for God to speak about me with a matter that would be recited. But I was hoping That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in a dream a vision in which God exonerated me. She said: By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not seek his place nor did any of the people of the house leave until God Almighty revealed to His Prophet, and he was seized by what he used to seize from the open space when the revelation came, until sweat would drip from him like pearls on a winter day from the weight of the words that were revealed to him. She said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was relieved, he was laughing, and the first word he spoke was to say, “Be of good cheer, O Aisha. God Almighty has acquitted you.” She said: My mother said to me, Get up to him. I said, “By God, I will not get up to him and I will not thank anyone but God Almighty. He is the One who revealed my innocence.” God Almighty revealed, Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you, all ten verses, and God revealed these verses about my innocence. She said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who used to spend on Mistah ibn Athatah because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: By God, I will never spend anything on him after what he said to Aisha. Then God Almighty revealed, And let not those among you who are endowed with virtue and wealth swear not to give to relatives and the needy and the emigrants in the land of their homes. The way of God, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that God should forgive you? And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Abu Bakr said: By God, I would like that God should forgive me. So he returned to Mistah the money he had been spending on him and said: By God, I will never take it away from him. Aisha said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked Zainab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), about my situation. He said: O Zainab, what did you know or see? She said: O Messenger of God, I protect my hearing and my sight. By God, I only know good. Aisha said: She was the one who used to be my equal among the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but God protected her through her piety. Her sister Hamna bint Jahsh began to fight on her behalf, and she was among those who perished. Ibn Shihab said: This is what has reached us about the situation of these people. It was included by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Ibn Ishaq narrated it in this way from Al-Zuhri. He also said: Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her. Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm Al-Ansari told me on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, similar to what was mentioned above. And God knows best. Then Al-Bukhari said, and Abu Usamah said, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: When he mentioned my affair that was mentioned and what I knew about it, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to deliver a sermon, and he bore witness and praised God and extolled Him as He deserves. Then he said: As for what follows, advise me regarding people who are my family, and by God I know nothing about my family except good, and I know nothing about my family except evil, and their children are those whom, by God, I know nothing about them except evil, and they never enter my house except when I am present, and I never go on a journey except that they are with me. So Sa`d bin Mu`adh Al-Ansari stood up and said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, give us permission to strike off their heads. Then a man from the Khazraj stood up, and Umm Hassan bin Thabit was from that man’s family, and he said: You have lied. By God, if they had been from the Aws, I would not have liked for their heads to be struck off, until there was almost evil between the Aws and the Khazraj in the mosque, and I did not know. So when it was evening of that day, I went out for some of my needs, and with me was Umm Mastih. Then she stumbled and said: “Cursed is Mistah.” I said to her: Which mother curses your son? She kept quiet. Then she stumbled a second time and said: Cursed is Mistah. I said to her: Which mother curses your son? Then she stumbled a third time and said: Cursed is Mistah. I rebuked her, and she said: By God, I only curse him because of you. I said: What is my business? She said: So she opened the hadith for me. I said: And this happened? She said: Yes, by God. I returned to my house as if I did not find much or little of what I had left for, and I became ill and said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Send me to my father’s house. He sent the boy with me, and I entered the house and found Umm Ruman downstairs and Abu Bakr upstairs reading. Umm Ruman said: What brought you here, my daughter? I told her and mentioned the hadith to her, and he did not do as much to her as he did to me. She said: My daughter, take it easy, for by God, there is rarely a beautiful woman with a man who loves her and has co-wives except that they envy her and gossip about her. I said: And my father knows about it? She said: Yes. I said: And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? She said: Yes, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I began to cry and weep. Abu Bakr heard my voice from above the house reciting, so he came down and said to my mother: What is the matter with her? She said: What was mentioned about her matter has reached her. His eyes may God be pleased with him filled with tears and he said: I swear to you, my daughter, to return to your house. So she returned. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to my house and asked about my maid. She said: No, by God, I did not know of any defect in her except that she used to sleep until a sheep would come in and eat its yeast or dough. One of his companions rebuked her and he said: Tell the truth to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they caused her to fall ill. She said: Glory be to God, by God, I did not know of anything about her except what a jeweler knows about red gold dust. report of the matter reached the man to whom it was said and he said: Glory be to God, by God I have never uncovered a woman’s private parts. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: He was martyred in the path of amusement. She said: My parents stayed with me the next morning and they did not leave until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon me after he had prayed the afternoon prayer. Then he entered and my parents surrounded me on my right and my left. He praised and thanked God, then he said: As for what follows, O Aisha, if you have committed a wrong or been unjust, then repent to God, for God accepts repentance from His servants. She said: A woman from the Ansar came and was sitting at the door. I said: Aren’t you ashamed to mention something in front of this woman? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) preached. I turned to my father and said to him: Answer him. He said: What should I say? I turned to my mother and said: Answer him. She said: What should I say? When they did not answer him, I testified, praised God and extolled Him as He deserves, then I said: As for what follows, by God, if I tell you that I did not do it, and God Almighty bears witness that I am truthful, that will not benefit me with you, for you have spoken it and your hearts have imbibed it. And if I tell you that I did do it, and God knows that I did not do it, you will say that she brought it upon herself, and by God I do not find an example for me and you. I sought the name of Jacob, but I could not find it except Abu Yusuf when he said, So be patient, and God is the sought for help against that which you describe. And God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, at that moment, so we were silent, and he was lifted from him, and I could see the joy on his face as he wiped his forehead and said, Be of good cheer, O Aisha, for God has revealed your innocence. She said: I was the most angry when my parents said to me, Rise up to him. I said, “No, by God, I will not rise up to him, nor will I praise him or you, but I praise God who revealed my innocence. You heard it and did not deny it or change it.” Aisha used to say: As for Zainab bint Jahsh, God protected her with her religion, and she only spoke good words. As for her sister Hamna bint Jahsh, she perished among those who perished. The one who spoke about him was Mistah and Hassan bin Thabit, and the hypocrite Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who was the one who used to bring him money and collect him, and he and Hamna were the ones who bore the brunt of it. She said: Abu Bakr swore that he would never benefit Mistah with anything, so God revealed: And let not those of virtue among you swear an oath meaning Abu Bakr and abundance is to give to relatives and the needy meaning Mistah until His saying: Would you not love that God should forgive you? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. Abu Bakr said: Yes, by God, O our Lord, we love that You should forgive us, and he returned to him with what he used to do.” This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it from this source, with a chain of transmission with a definitive form, on the authority of Abu Usamah Hammad bin Usamah, one of the trustworthy imams. Ibn Jarir narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Sufyan bin Wakee’ on the authority of Abu Osama narrated it in full, like it or something similar. Ibn Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Ashja on the authority of Abu Osama in part. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: When my excuse was revealed from the sky, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me and informed me of it, so I said: We praise God, not you. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Uday told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Umrah also, on the authority of Aisha, who said: When my excuse was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up and mentioned it and recited the Qur’an. When it was revealed, he ordered two men and a woman to be flogged. It was included by the four scholars of Sunan, and Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith. Abu Dawud mentioned their names as Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Athatah, and Hamna bint Jahsh. So there are multiple chains of transmission on the authority of the Mother of the Believers Aisha may God be pleased with her in the Musnads, Sahihs, Sunans, and elsewhere. It was narrated from the hadith of her mother, Umm Ruman, may God be pleased with her. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Asim told us, Hisin told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Umm Ruman, who said: While I was with Aisha, a woman from the Ansar entered upon us and said: May God do this to her son and that. Aisha said: Why? She said: He was among those who narrated the hadith. She said: Which hadith? She said: So and so. She said: Has this reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? She said: Yes. She said: Has this reached Abu Bakr? She said: Yes. Aisha may God be pleased with her fell unconscious, and she did not regain consciousness until she was suffering from a fever with a chill, so I got up and covered her. She said: Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and said: What is the matter with her? I said: O Messenger of God, she has a fever with a chill. He said: Perhaps it is in a hadith he spoke about. She said: Aisha sat up straight for him and said: By God, if I swear to you, you will not believe me, and if I apologize to you, you will not excuse me. My example and yours are like that of Jacob and his sons when he said: So be patient, most fittingly, and God is the sought for help against that which you describe. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and God revealed her excuse. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned with Abu Bakr, and he entered and said: O Aisha, God has revealed your excuse. She said: Praise be to God, not to you. Abu Bakr said to her: You say this to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: Yes. She said: Among those who narrated this hadith was a man who was supported by Abu Bakr, and he swore that he would not connect with him, so God revealed: And let not those among you who are endowed with wealth and abundance swear not to give them their children to the end of the verse, and Abu Bakr said: Yes, so connect with him. Al-Bukhari is the only one who narrated it, not Muslim, via the chain of transmission of Hisin. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Musa bin Ismail, on the authority of Abu Uwanah, and on the authority of Muhammad bin Salam, on the authority of Muhammad bin Fadil, both on the authority of Hisin, with the following wording: And in the wording of Abu Uwanah: Umm Ruman told me. This is clear evidence that Masruq heard it from her. A group of hadith masters denied this, including al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, because the historians mentioned that she died during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Khatib said: Masruq used to send it out and say: Umm Ruman was asked, and he would quote it, so perhaps some of them wrote: She was asked with a thousand, and the narrator thought that she was asked, so he thought it was connected. Al-Khatib said: Al-Bukhari narrated it in this way, but its defect was not clear to him. So he said, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who brought forth the slander meaning lies, slander and calumny are a group meaning a group among you. Do not think it is evil for you meaning O family of Abu Bakr. Rather, it is good for you meaning in this world and the hereafter. It is a tongue of truth in this world and an elevation of status in the hereafter and a manifestation of their honor through God the Almighty’s care for Aisha, the mother of the believers, may God be pleased with her, as God revealed her innocence in the Noble Qur’an: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it verse. For this reason, when Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him and her, entered upon her while she was dying, he said to her: Be of good tidings, for you are the wife of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he loved you and did not marry a virgin other than you, and he revealed your innocence from the heavens. Ibn Jarir said in his interpretation: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Wasiti told us, Jaafar ibn Awn told us, on the authority of al-Mu’alla ibn Irfan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh, who said: Aisha and Zainab, may God be pleased with them, boasted. Zainab said: I am the one whose marriage was revealed from the heaven. Aisha said: I am the one whose excuse was revealed in the Book of God when Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal carried me on the mount. Zainab said to her: O Aisha, what did you say when you mounted it? She said: I said: God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. She said: I said the word of the believers. And the Almighty’s saying: For every person among them is what he has earned of sin meaning, for every one who spoke about this issue and accused the Mother of the Believers Aisha may God be pleased with her of something shameful, there is a great share of punishment. And he among them who bore the greater part thereof It was said that he began with him, and it was said that he was the one who collected it, gathered it, spread it, and propagated it. For him is a great punishment meaning for that. Then the majority are of the opinion that what is meant by this is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may God curse and curse him, and he is the one who was mentioned explicitly in the hadith. This was said by Mujahid and others. It was also said that what is meant by it is Hassan ibn Thabit, and this is a strange opinion. If it were not for the fact that it appears in Sahih al-Bukhari, which indicates this, there would not have been much benefit in including it, because he was one of the Companions who had virtues, merits, and achievements, and the best of his achievements was that he used to defend the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) with his poetry, and he is the one to whom the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Incite them, and Gabriel is with you. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha on the authority of Masruq who said: I was with Aisha may God be pleased with her when Hassan ibn Thabit entered, so I ordered that a pillow be thrown for him. When he came out, I said to Aisha: What are you doing with this man? Meaning, he enters upon you. In another narration, she was told: Do you give him permission to enter upon you, when God said: And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof will have a great punishment. She said: What punishment is more severe than blindness? He had lost his sight, so perhaps God will make that the great punishment. Then she said that he was defending the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). In another narration, he recited to her a poem praising her when he entered upon her, and he said: Razan's horse is not suspiciously heavy and becomes hungry from the meat of the ignorant She said: As for you, you are not like that. In another narration: But you are not like that. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah told us, Salamah bin Alqamah told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: I have never heard of poetry better than the poetry of Hassan, and I have never recited it except that I hoped for Paradise for him. His saying to Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib: I satirized Muhammad, so I responded to him, and that is the reward from God My father, his father, and my honor are a protection for Muhammad’s honor from you. You insult him, and you are not his equal? May God sacrifice you both for the sake of your best interests. My tongue is strict and flawless, and my sea is untroubled by buckets. It was said: O Mother of the Believers, is this not idle talk? She said: No, idle talk is what is said in the presence of women. It was said: Did not God say: And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof will have a great punishment. She said: Has not a great punishment befallen him? Has he not lost his sight and been struck by the sword? She meant the blow that Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal as-Sulami struck him when he heard that he was speaking about that, so he struck him with the sword and almost killed him.
12:19: God Almighty says, informing about what happened to Joseph, peace be upon him, when his brothers threw him in and left him in that well alone and isolated. He remained in the well for three days, according to what Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When his brothers threw him in, they sat around the well that day, watching what he would do and what would be done to him. Then God sent a car to him, so they descended close to that well, and they sent their water-drawer, who was the one who would ask for water for them. When he came to that well and lowered his bucket into it, Joseph, peace be upon him, clung to it, so he pulled him out and was happy with him, and said: Good report! This is a boy. Some of the reciters read Ya Bushrai, and al-Suddi claimed that it is the name of a man who called out to him when the man lowered his bucket, informing him that he had found a boy. This statement by al-Suddi is strange because he did not precede him in interpreting this reading in this way except in a narration from Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Rather, the meaning of the reading in this manner goes back to the other reading, and he would have added the good report to himself and deleted the ya of addition, and he meant it as the Arabs say: Ya Nafs, be patient and Ya Ghalam, come, by deleting the letter of addition. The kasra and the nominative are permissible in that case, and this is from him, and the other reading interprets it as Ya Bushrai, and God knows best. And his saying: And they concealed him as merchandise means that the people who came from the rest of the caravan concealed him and said: We bought him and bought him from the owners of the water for fear that they would share in it with them if they knew about him. Mujahid, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir said: This is one saying. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His saying: And they concealed him as merchandise means that Joseph’s brothers concealed his affair and concealed that he was their brother. Joseph concealed his affair for fear that his brothers would kill him, and he chose to sell him, so his brothers mentioned him to the people who came, so he called out to his companions: Good report! This is a boy to be sold, so his brothers sold him. And His saying: And God is Knowing of what they do means He is Knowing of what Joseph’s brothers and those who bought him did, and He is able to change that and prevent it, but He has wisdom and a previous destiny, so He left that to carry out what He had decreed and decided. “Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.” In this there is an allusion to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an announcement to him that I am aware of the harm your people have done to you, and I am able to denounce them, but I will grant them respite and then I will make you the outcome and the judgement over them, just as I made Joseph the judgement and the outcome over his brothers. And His statement: And they sold him for a cheap price, for a few dirhams, God the Almighty says: And his brothers sold him for a small price. This was said by Mujahid and Ikrimah. And bakhs means deficiency, as God the Almighty said: So he fears neither loss nor burden, meaning his brothers compensated him for a less than small price, and despite that they were among those who were indifferent to him, meaning they had no desire for him. Rather, if they had asked him for nothing, they would have answered. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: The pronoun in His statement: And they sold him refers to Joseph’s brothers. Qatada said: Rather, it refers to the caravan. The first is stronger, because His statement: And they were among those who were indifferent to him refers to his brothers, not those caravans, because the caravans were happy with him and considered him a commodity, and if they had been indifferent to him, they would not have bought him. So it is more likely from this that the pronoun in sold him refers to his brothers. It was said: What is meant by His statement bakhs is the forbidden. It was said: Injustice, even if this is the case, it is not what is meant here, because it is known and known by everyone that his price is forbidden in every case and for everyone because he is a prophet, son of a prophet, son of a prophet, son of the friend of the Most Merciful, so he is the generous son of the generous son of the generous son of the generous. Rather, what is meant here by cheapness is the deficient or the counterfeit or both, meaning that they are his brothers and they sold him, and with this at a lower price, and for this reason he said counted dirhams, so Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: They sold him for twenty dirhams, and Ibn Abbas, Nawf Al-Bakali, Al-Suddi, Qatadah, and Atiyah Al-Awfi said the same, and he added that they divided it two dirhams each. Mujahid said: Twenty-two dirhams. Muhammad bin Ishaq and Ikrimah said: Forty dirhams. Ad-Dahhak said in his statement: And they were among those who were ascetics in him that is because they did not know of his prophethood and his status with God, the Almighty, and Mujahid said: When they sold him, they followed them and said to them: Make sure that he does not run away, until they stopped him in Egypt and he said: Who will buy me and give me good report? The king bought him and he was a Muslim.

12:21: God the Almighty tells us of His kindness to Joseph, peace be upon him, that He provided for him the one who bought him from Egypt, so that he took care of him and honored him, and recommended him to his family, and saw goodness and righteousness in him, so he said to his wife, Honor his stay; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son. The one who bought him from Egypt was its Aziz, who was the minister. Al-Awfi told us on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and his name was Qutfir. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: His name was Atfir ibn Ruhaib, who was the Aziz, and he was in charge of the treasuries of Egypt. The king at that time was Rayyan ibn al-Walid, a man from the Amalekites. He said: His wife's name was Ra'il bint Ra'il. Another said: Her name was Zulaykha. Muhammad ibn Ishaq also said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The one who sold him in Egypt was Malik ibn Da'r ibn Buwayb ibn Anqa ibn Madyan ibn Ibrahim, and God knows best. Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he said: The most perceptive of people are three: the Aziz of Egypt when he said to his wife: Make his stay honorable, and the woman who said to her father: O my father, hire him verse, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he appointed Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them both, as his successor. God Almighty says: Just as We saved Joseph from his brothers, Thus did We establish Joseph in the land meaning the land of Egypt, and that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: It is an interpretation of the vision, And God is predominant over His affair, meaning if He wants something, He cannot be prevented, hindered, or opposed. Rather, He is predominant over everything else. Saeed bin Jubair said about His statement, And God is predominant over His affair, meaning He does whatever He wills. And His statement, But most people do not know, means they do not know His wisdom in His creation, His gentleness, and His doing of what He wills. And His statement, And when he reached his maturity, meaning Joseph, peace be upon him, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, meaning the prophethood that He bestowed upon him among those peoples. And thus do We reward the doers of good, meaning that he was a doer of good in his work, working in obedience to God Almighty. There is a difference of opinion regarding the amount of time in which he reached his maturity. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: Thirty-three years. And from Ibn Abbas: Thirty-something. Ad-Dahhak said: Twenty. And Al-Hasan said: Forty years. And Ikrimah said: Twenty-five years. And As-Suddi said: Thirty years. Saeed bin Jubair said: Eighteen years. Imam Malik, Rabia bin Zaid bin Aslam and Al-Shaabi said: The most severe is patience, and other things were said, and God knows best.
