12:23: The Almighty tells about the wife of Al-Aziz, in whose house Joseph was in Egypt, and her husband had commanded her to treat him with respect, so she tried to seduce him, that is, she tried to seduce him and invited him to her, because she loved him intensely for his beauty, goodness and splendor, so that made her beautify herself for him and closed the doors on him and invited him to herself, and she said, 'Come to me,' but he refused that vehemently, and he said, 'God forbid! Indeed, my Lord has made my stay good' and they used to call the great master Lord, meaning, your husband is my Lord, has made my stay good, that is, my home, and has treated me well, so I will not meet him with immorality with his family, Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed, said Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others. The reciters differed regarding his saying: Come to me, as many recited it with a fatha on the ha', a sukoon on the ya' and a fatha on the ta', and Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: Its meaning is that she invites him to herself. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Hayt lak means come to you. This is what Zur bin Hubaish, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said. Amr bin Ubaid said on the authority of Al-Hasan: It is a word in Syriac, meaning upon you. Al-Suddi said: Hayt lak means come to you, and it is in Coptic. Mujahid said: It is an Arabic language in which you call upon Him. Al-Bukhari said: “Ikrimah said: “Hayt lak” means come to you in Hawran. This is how he mentioned it in a suspended form. Imam Jaafar bin Jarir narrated it: Ahmad bin Sahl al-Wasiti told me, Qara bin Isa told us, al-Nadr bin Arabi al-Jazari told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Hayt lak, he said: Come to you. He said: It is in Hawran. Abu Ubaid al-Qasim bin Salam said: Al-Kisa’i used to narrate this reading, meaning Hayt lak, and he said: It is a language of the people of Hawran that was passed on to the people of Hijaz, and its meaning is come. Abu Ubaidah said: I asked a knowledgeable sheikh from the people of Hawran, and he mentioned that it is their language that he knows. Imam Ibn Jarir cited as evidence for this reading the words of the poet to Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Inform the Commander of the Faithful of the harm to Iraq if we come Iraq and its people are yours, so come and come He says: Come and approach. Others read it as hay’at laka with a kasra on the ha’, with a hamza and a damma on the ta’, meaning it was prepared for you from the saying of the speaker: hay’at bi-al-amr ahyi hay’at. Among those who narrated this reading from him are: Ibn Abbas, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Wa’il, Ikrimah and Qatadah, and all of them interpreted it as meaning it was prepared for you. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Amr and al-Kisa’i rejected this reading. Abdullah ibn Ishaq read: hay’at with a fatha on the ha’ and a kasra on the ta’, and it is strange. Others, including the majority of the people of Madinah, read hay’at with a fatha on the ha’ and a damma on the ta’, and he recited the words of the poet: My people are not the farthest away if a caller from the tribe says: Hit Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri informed us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: Ibn Mas’ud said, after hearing the reciters: I heard them close together, so recite as you have been taught, and beware of exaggeration and disagreement. It is like one of you saying: Come and come. Then Abdullah recited: Hayt laka, and he said: O Abu Abdul Rahman, some people recite it as Hayt. Abdullah said: I prefer to recite it as you have been taught. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told me, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: Abdullah said: Hayt laka, and Masruq said to him: Some people recite it as Hayt laka, so he said: Leave me, for I prefer to recite as you have been taught. He also said: Al-Muthanna told me, Adam ibn Abi Iyas told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Hayt laka with the accusative of the ha’ and the ta’, and without the hamza. Others said: Hayt laka with the kasra of the ha’, the sukoon of the ya’, and the damma of the ta’. Abu Ubaid Muammar bin Al-Muthanna said: “Hayt is not dual, plural, or feminine. Rather, it is used to address all of them with one word, so it is said: Hayt laka, Hayt lakum, Hayt lakumma, Hayt lakuna, Hayt lakuna, Hayt lakuna.”
12:24: People's statements and expressions differed in this regard. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair and a group of the Salaf in this regard, what was narrated by Ibn Jarir and others, and God knows best. It was said: What is meant by his intentions are the thoughts of his soul, narrated by Al-Baghawi from some of the people of investigation. Then Al-Baghawi included here the hadith of Abd Al-Razzaq from Muammar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God the Most High says: If My servant intends to do a good deed, write it down for him as a good deed. If he does it, write it down for him as ten times its like. If he intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, write it down as a good deed, for he left it out of My reward. If he does it, write it down as one like it." This hadith was narrated in the two Sahihs and it has many wordings, this is one of them. It was said: He intended to hit her. It was also said: He wished for her as a wife. It was said: He intended to do it had he not seen the proof of his Lord, meaning he did not intend to do it. This statement is questionable in terms of Arabic, as narrated by Ibn Jarir and others. As for the proof that he saw, there are also statements about it. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, Saeed, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Muhammad bin Sirin, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Salih, Ad-Dahhak, Muhammad bin Ishaq and others: He saw the image of his father Jacob, peace be upon him, biting his finger with his mouth. It was said about him in a narration: He struck Joseph in the chest. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He saw the shadow of the king, meaning his master. Muhammad bin Ishaq said the same in what he narrated on the authority of some of them: It was only the shadow of his master Qutfir when he approached the door. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Waki` told us, on the authority of Abu Mawdud, I heard from Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, he said: Yusuf raised his head to the ceiling of the house, and there was written on the wall of the house: “And do not approach adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way.” Abu Ma`shar al-Madani narrated it in this way on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b. Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Nafi` ibn Yazid told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, he said: I heard al-Qurazi say: Among the proof that Yusuf saw were three verses from the Book of God: Verily, over you are guardians 1:13, and His statement: And you are not in any affair 1:13, and His statement: Then is He who stands over every soul for what it has earned? 1:13. Nafi` said: I heard Abu Hilal say the same as al-Qurazi, and he added a fourth verse: And do not approach adultery. Al-Awza`i said: He saw a verse from the Book of God on the wall forbidding him from that. Ibn Jarir said: The correct thing to say is that he saw a sign from the signs of God that deterred him from what he was about to do. It is possible that it was an image of Jacob, or an image of the king, or what he saw written as a deterrent from that, but there is no conclusive proof to specify any of that, so the correct thing to say is as God the Most High said. And His statement: Thus did We turn away from him evil and immorality means that just as We showed him a proof that turned him away from what he was doing, thus did We purify him from evil and immorality in all his affairs: Indeed, he is of Our chosen, purified, chosen, chosen, and good servants, meaning one of the chosen, purified, chosen, and good ones, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him.
12:25: God Almighty tells of their situation when they went out racing to the door: Joseph was running away, and the woman was looking for him to return home. She caught up with him while doing so, and she grabbed his shirt from behind. She lost it terribly. It is said that it fell off him, and Joseph continued running away, and she was following him. They found her master, who was her husband, at the door. Then she got out of what she was in with her cunning and deceit, and said to her husband, evading her punishment and accusing Joseph of her illness: What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your family except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment? That is, he be beaten severely and painfully. Then Joseph, peace be upon him, triumphed with the truth, and he was innocent of what she had accused him of of treason, and he said, She sought to seduce me for my soul, and he mentioned that she followed him, luring him towards her until she tore his shirt. And a witness from her family testified that if his shirt was torn from the front, meaning from the front, then she is telling the truth, meaning in her statement that he sought to seduce her, because when he called her and she refused, she pushed him in the chest, she lost his shirt, so what she said would be valid. But if his shirt was torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful, and that would be as happened when he fled from her and she sought him, she grabbed his shirt from behind to bring him back to her, she lost his shirt from behind, and they differed about this witness: was he young or old? According to two sayings of the scholars of the Salaf, Abd al-Razzaq said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And a witness from among her people testified, Dhu Lihyad said, and al-Thawri said, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Mulaykah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He was one of the king’s confidants. And Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said the same: He was a man. And Zayd ibn Aslam al-Suddi said: He was her cousin. And Ibn Abbas said: He was one of the king’s confidants. And Ibn Ishaq mentioned that Zulaykha was the niece of King Rayyan ibn al-Walid. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And a witness from among her people testified, he said: He was a boy in the cradle. It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Hilal bin Yasaf, Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim that he was a boy in the house. Ibn Jarir chose it. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet was narrated on this matter. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Affan told us, Hammad told us, he is Ibn Salamah, Ata bin As-Sa’ib told me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Four spoke while they were young, and he mentioned among them the witness of Joseph. It was narrated by others on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ata, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “Four spoke while they were young: the son of the hairdresser of Pharaoh’s daughter, the witness of Joseph, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus, son of Mary.” Laith bin Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid: It was from the command of God Almighty, and he was not human. This is a strange statement. And His saying: And when he saw his shirt torn from the back meaning when her husband was certain of Joseph’s truthfulness and her lying in what she had slandered and accused him of, he said, ‘Indeed, it is of your plot’ meaning that this slander and defamation with which she had tarnished this young man’s honor is part of your plot, Indeed, your plot is great. Then he said, commanding Joseph, peace be upon him, to conceal what had happened, Joseph, turn away from this meaning, ignore this completely, meaning, do not mention it to anyone. And ask forgiveness for your sin, he said to his wife, although he was easygoing and gentle, or he excused her because she saw something she could not bear to avoid, so he said to her: Seek forgiveness for your sin, meaning what happened from you in wanting evil for this young man and then accusing him of something he was innocent of. For you were among the sinners.

12:30: God Almighty tells us that the report of Joseph and the wife of Al-Aziz spread in the city, which is Egypt, until people talked about it. And the women of the city said, like the women of the nobles and princes, denouncing the wife of Al-Aziz, who is the minister, and blaming her for that, The wife of Al-Aziz is trying to seduce her young man, meaning she is trying to get her slave to have sex with her and inviting him to herself. He has overwhelmed her with love, meaning his love has reached the pericardium of her heart, which is its covering. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Passion is deadly love, and passion is less than that, and the pericardium is the veil of the heart. Indeed, we see her in manifest error, meaning in her actions of loving her young man and her attempts to seduce him. But when she heard of their plot, some of them said: Because of their words, love took her away. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Rather, they heard of Joseph’s beauty, so they wanted to see him, so they said that in order to be able to see and witness him. Then, she sent to them, meaning she invited them to her house to host them, and she prepared for them a reclining place. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi and others said: It is a gathering in which bedding, pillows and food are prepared, including things that are cut with knives, such as citrons and the like. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And she gave each one of them a knife. This was a trick from her and a confrontation with them in their deception of seeing him. And she said, ‘Come out to them.’ This is because she had hidden him in another place. So when he came out, they saw him and magnified him. That is, they magnified his status and revered his esteem. They began to cut their hands in astonishment at seeing him, and they thought that they were cutting citrons with knives. What is meant is that they cut their hands with them, as was said by more than one person. Mujahid and Qatadah said: They cut their hands until they threw them away. And God knows best. More than one person has mentioned that she said to them after they had eaten and were satisfied, then she placed a citron in their hands and gave each one of them a knife: Would you like to look at Joseph? They said: Yes. So she sent to him ordering him to come out to them. When they saw him, they began to cut their hands. Then she ordered him to return so that they could see him coming and going. So he returned while they were cutting their hands. When they felt the pain, they began to wail. She said: You did this because of a single look, so how can I be blamed? “And they said, ‘God forbid! This is not a human being. This is nothing but a noble angel.’” Then they said to her, “We do not see any blame on you after what we have seen, because they have not seen anyone like him or even close to him. He, peace be upon him, had been given half of his beauty, as was confirmed in the authentic hadith in the hadith of the Night Journey, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Joseph, peace be upon him, in the third heaven. He said, “And behold, he had been given half of his beauty.” Hammad ibn Salamah said, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Joseph and his mother were given half of their beauty.’” Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said, Joseph and his mother were given one-third of their beauty. Abu Ishaq also said, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said, Joseph’s face was like lightning, and when a woman came to him for a need, she would cover her face for fear of being tempted by him. Al-Hasan al-Basri narrated it in a mursal form on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Joseph and his mother were given one-third of the beauty of the people of this world, and the people were given two-thirds, or he said: Joseph and his mother were given two-thirds and the people were given one-third. Sufyan said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Rabia al-Jurashi, who said: Beauty was divided in half, so Joseph and his mother Sarah were given half of beauty, and the other half was given to the rest of creation. Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Suhayli said: Its meaning is that Joseph, peace be upon him, was half as handsome as Adam, peace be upon him, for God created Adam with His own hand in the most perfect and best form, and there was no one among his descendants who could match him in beauty. Joseph had been given half of his beauty, so these women said when they saw him, God forbid. Mujahid and more than one other said: God forbid, This is not a human being, and some of them read, This is not a human being, meaning someone bought with a purchase. “This is nothing but a noble angel. She said, “This is that for which you blamed me,” she said this, apologizing to them that this man truly deserved to be loved for his beauty and perfection. And I did indeed seek to seduce him, but he refused, meaning he refused. Some of them said: When they saw his apparent beauty, she told them about his good qualities that were hidden from them, which are chastity along with this beauty, then she said threatening him, And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be among the debased. At that time, Joseph, peace be upon him, sought refuge from their evil and their plotting, and He said, ‘My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me,’ meaning the immorality. And if You do not avert from me their plotting, I will incline toward them. That is, if You leave me to myself, I have no power over it and I do not possess any harm or benefit for it except through Your power and strength. You are the one sought for help and upon You is reliance, so do not leave me to myself, incline toward them and be among the ignorant. So his Lord responded to him, the verse. Al-Suddi said: The reason the king imprisoned them was that he thought they were conspiring to poison him in his food and drink. Joseph, peace be upon him, was known in prison for his generosity, honesty, truthfulness, good manners, and frequent worship, may God's prayers and peace be upon him. He was also known for his knowledge of interpretation and kindness to the people of the prison, visiting their sick, and fulfilling their rights. When these two young men entered the prison, they became close to him and loved him intensely, and they said to him: By God, we have loved you excessively. He said: May God bless you both. No one loved me except that harm came to me because of his love. My aunt loved me, and harm came to me because of her. My father loved me, and I was harmed because of him. The wife of Al-Aziz loved me, and so did I. They said: By God, we cannot do anything but that. Then they saw a dream, and the cupbearer saw that he was pressing wine, meaning grapes. And this is how it is in the recitation of Abdullah bin Masoud: I see myself pressing grapes. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sinan, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Zaid ibn Wahb, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, that he read it: I press grapes. Ad-Dahhak said regarding his statement, I see myself pressing wine, meaning grapes. He said: The people of Oman call grapes wine. Ikrimah said: He said to him: I saw in a dream that I planted a grape seed, and it grew and clusters came out of it. I pressed them and then gave them to the king to drink. He said: You will remain in prison for three days, then you will come out and give him wine to drink. The other, the baker, said: “I see myself carrying bread on my head from which birds eat. Tell us its interpretation,” the verse. What is well-known among most of them is what we mentioned, that they saw a dream and asked for its interpretation. Ibn Jarir said: We were told by Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid, who said: We were told by Jarir on the authority of Amara bin Al-Qa’qa’ on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The two companions of Joseph did not see anything, they only dreamed of him to test him.
12:37: Joseph, peace be upon him, tells them that whatever dream they see in their dreams, he knows its interpretation and tells them its interpretation before it happens. That is why he said: No food will come to you that you are provided with, except that I will inform you of its interpretation. Mujahid said: No food will come to you that you are provided with in your day except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. Al-Suddi said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala told us, Muhammad bin Yazid, his sheikh, told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Thauban, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I do not know, perhaps Joseph, peace be upon him, was averse to it while he was like that, because I find in the Book of God when he said to the two men: No food will come to you that you are provided with, except that I will inform you of its interpretation, he said: If the food is sweet or bitter, he will be averse to it at that time. Then Ibn Abbas said: He only knew, so he taught, and this is a strange trace. Then he said: This is only from God’s teaching me, because I avoided the religion of the disbelievers in God and the Last Day, so they do not expect reward or punishment in the afterlife. And I followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob the verse, he says: I abandoned the path of disbelief and polytheism, and followed the path of these messengers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all, and this is the state of the one who follows the path of guidance, and follows the path of the messengers, and turns away from the path of the misguided, for God guides his heart, and teaches him what he did not know, and makes him an imam to be followed in goodness, and a caller to the path of righteousness. “It was not for us to associate anything with God. That is from the grace of God upon us and upon mankind.” This is monotheism, which is the acknowledgment that there is no god but God alone, with no partner. From the grace of God upon us meaning He revealed it to us and commanded us to do it. And upon the people since We made them callers to that but most of the people are not grateful meaning they do not recognize the blessing of God upon them by sending messengers to them, rather they exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of destruction. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to make the grandfather a father and say: By God, whoever he wants, I will curse him at the Black Stone, God did not mention a grandfather or a grandmother. God Almighty said, meaning in relation to Joseph: And I followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

12:39: Then Joseph, peace be upon him, addressed the two young men and called them to worship God alone, with no partner, and to abandon the idols that their people worshipped. He said: Are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing? That is, the One to whom all things are humbled for the glory of His majesty and the greatness of His power. Then he explained to them that what they worship and call gods is nothing but ignorance on their part, and a naming of their own accord, which their successors received from their predecessors, and that there is no basis for that from God. For this reason, he said: God has not sent down any authority for it, that is, no proof or evidence. Then he informed them that the judgment, disposition, will, and dominion are all for God, and He has commanded all of His servants to worship none but Him. Then God Almighty said: That is the right religion, that is, this that I call you to, of monotheism and sincerity in action for Him, is the straight religion that God has commanded, and for which He has sent down the proof and evidence that He loves and is pleased. But most people do not know, that is, for this reason most of them Polytheists, And most people, even if you strive hard, are not believers. So they repeated it to him, so he repeated the sermon to them. There is a consideration in what he said, because he had promised them at first to interpret it, but he made their question to him a matter of respect and reverence and a connection and reason to call them to monotheism and Islam, because he saw in their nature the acceptance of goodness and turning to it and listening to it. For this reason, when he finished calling them, he began to interpret their dream without repeating the question, so he said:

12:41: He said to them, O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give his master wine to drink, and he is the one who saw that he was pressing wine, but he did not specify him lest the other one be sad, and for this reason he made him ambiguous in his statement, As for the other, he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head, and he is in the same matter that he saw that he was carrying bread on his head, then he informed them that this had been completed, and it will inevitably happen, because the vision of a flying man is not interpreted, but if it is interpreted, it will happen. Al-Thawri said: On the authority of Ammarah ibn al-Qa'qa', on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: When they said what they said and he informed them, they said: We did not see anything, so he said: The matter about which you are asking has been decided. Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated it on the authority of Ammarah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, and Mujahid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others interpreted it in the same way. The gist of it is that whoever dreams of falsehood and interprets it, then he is obligated to interpret it, and God Almighty knows best. It was mentioned in the noble hadith that Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Muawiyah bin Haidah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The vision is for a flying man as long as it is not interpreted. If it is interpreted, it will come true.” And in Musnad Abi Ya’la, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, The vision is for the first one to interpret it.
12:42: And when Joseph, peace be upon him, thought that the cupbearer was safe, Joseph said to him secretly from the other - and God knows best - so that he would not feel that he was the one crucified - he said to him, Mention me to your Lord, meaning: Mention my story to your Lord, who is the King. So the one who was recommended forgot to mention that to his master, the King, and it was among the tricks of Satan so that the Prophet of God would not be released from prison. This is correct, that the pronoun in his saying, So Satan made him forget to mention his Lord, refers to the one who was saved, as Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said. It is said that the pronoun refers to Joseph, peace be upon him. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and others. Ibn Jarir attributed a hadith here and said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Amr ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Yazid, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If he - meaning Joseph - had not said the word that he said, he would not have remained in prison as long as he remained seeking relief from other than God. This hadith is very weak, because Sufyan ibn Wakee’ is weak, and Ibrahim ibn Yazid, who is Al-Khawzi, is also weaker than him. It has been narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatadah in mursal form from each of them, and these mursals here are not accepted if the mursal is accepted from where it is in a place other than this, and God knows best. As for the word bad’a, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It is between three and nine. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Job remained in affliction for seven, Joseph in prison for seven, and Nebuchadnezzar was tortured for seven. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, He remained in prison for a few years, meaning twelve years. Ad-Dahhak said: fourteen years.
12:43: This vision from the King of Egypt was what God Almighty had decreed was the reason for Joseph, peace be upon him, to be released from prison, honored and respected. The king saw this vision, and it terrified him and he was amazed by its matter and what its interpretation would be. So he gathered the priests, the shoemakers, the leaders of his state, and his princes and told them what he had seen and asked them about its interpretation, but they did not know that, and they apologized to him that it was confused dreams, meaning a mixture of dreams that this vision of yours required. And we are not knowledgeable about the interpretation of dreams, meaning if it had been a true vision of a mixture, we would not have had knowledge of its interpretation, which is its explanation. Then he remembered the one who had escaped from those two young men who were in prison with Joseph, and Satan had made him forget what Joseph had instructed him to do about mentioning his matter to the king. Then he remembered after a period, meaning a period, and some of them read after his mother, meaning after forgetting, so he said to them, meaning to the king and those whom he had gathered for that, I will inform you of its interpretation, meaning the interpretation of this The dream, So send means send to Joseph the Truthful to prison, and the meaning of the words is that they sent him and he came to him, and he said: Joseph, O truthful one, give us your advice and he mentioned the dream that the king saw, then Joseph, peace be upon him, told him its interpretation without reprimanding the young man for forgetting what he had commanded him, and without stipulating that he should leave before that, but he said: You shall sow for seven years in succession meaning that fertility and rain will come to you for seven consecutive years, so he interpreted the cows as years because they plow the land from which fruits and crops are harvested, and they are the green ears of corn, then he guided them to what they should prepare for those years, so he said: So whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear except a little of what you eat meaning whatever you harvested in these seven fertile years, save it in its ear so that it will be more lasting for it and further from it quickly spoiling except for the amount that you eat, and let it be little by little, do not be extravagant with it so that you may benefit in the seven difficult years, and they are the seven years of drought that follow these seven consecutive years, and they are the lean cows Those who eat the fat, because in the years of drought what they gathered in the years of fertility is eaten, and they are the dry ears of corn, and he informed them that they do not grow anything, and what they sow they do not return to anything, and for this reason he said: They eat what you have put in advance for them except a little of what you store. Then he gave them good report after the successive year of drought that after that there will be a year in which people will be given relief, meaning rain will come to them and the land will be abundant, and people will squeeze what they used to squeeze according to their custom of oil and the like, and sugar and the like, until some of them said: milking milk is also included in it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And in it they squeeze means they milk.

He only asked him to make him the treasury of the earth, which are the pyramids in which the crops are collected, because of the years that they will face, which he informed them about, so that he may dispose of them in the most cautious, best, and wisest manner. So he was granted that out of desire for him and honor for him. For this reason, the Most High said:
12:56: God Almighty says: And thus We established Joseph in the land meaning the land of Egypt, to settle therein wherever he willed. Al-Suddi and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: He disposed of it as he wished. Ibn Jarir said: He takes from it a home wherever he wishes after the distress, imprisonment and captivity, We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not waste the reward of the doers of good. That is, We did not waste Joseph’s patience in the harm of his brothers and his patience in imprisonment because of the wife of the Aziz, so God Almighty followed him with peace, victory and support, “And We do not waste the reward of the doers of good. And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and fear God.” God Almighty informs that what God Almighty has stored for His Prophet Joseph, peace be upon him, in the Hereafter is greater, more numerous and more sublime than what He granted him of control and influence in this world, like His saying regarding Solomon, peace be upon him: “This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account. And indeed, with Us is nearness to him and a good place of return.” The point is that Joseph, peace be upon him, was appointed by the King of Egypt, Rayyan bin Al-Walid, as a minister in the land of Egypt in place of the one he bought from Egypt, the husband of the woman who tried to seduce him, and the kingdom converted to Islam at the hands of Joseph, peace be upon him, as Mujahid said. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When Joseph said to the king: “Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I am a knowing guardian,” the king said: I have done so. So he appointed him, as they mentioned, to the position of Atfir, and removed Atfir from what he had been in charge of. God Almighty says: “And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good.” He said: It was mentioned to me - and God knows best - that Atfir died during those nights, and that King Rayyan bin Al-Walid married Joseph to Atfir’s wife Ra’il, and that when she entered upon him he said to her: Is this not better than what you wanted? He said: They claim that she said: O friend, do not blame me, for I was a woman as you see, beautiful, lovely, and soft in a kingdom and a world, and my companion did not come to women, and I was as God made you in your beauty and appearance as you saw. They claim that he found her a virgin, so he had intercourse with her, and she bore him two men: Ephraim bin Yusuf, and Misha bin Yusuf. Ephraim had Nun, the father of Joshua bin Nun, and Rahmah, the wife of Job, peace be upon him. Al-Fudayl bin Iyad said: The wife of Al-Aziz stopped on the side of the road until Joseph passed by, and she said: Praise be to God who made slaves kings through his obedience, and kings slaves through his disobedience.

12:58: Al-Suddi, Muhammad bin Ishaq, and other commentators mentioned that the reason why Joseph's brothers came to Egypt was that when Joseph, peace be upon him, took over the ministry in Egypt and the seven fertile years passed, then the seven barren years followed, and famine spread throughout the land of Egypt and reached the land of Canaan, which is where Jacob, peace be upon him, and his sons were. At that time, Joseph, peace be upon him, took precautions for the people regarding their crops and collected them in the best way, so a great sum and many enormous gifts were obtained from that, and people came to him from all the regions and dealings, buying for themselves and their families, so he did not give a man more than a camel's load in a year, and he, peace be upon him, did not satisfy himself, and he and the king and their soldiers did not eat except one meal in the middle of the day, so that the people would be satisfied with what they had in their hands for the period of seven years, and it was a mercy from God to the people of Egypt. And what some commentators mentioned that he sold them in the first year for money, and in the second for goods, and in the third for so-and-so, and in the fourth for so-and-so, until he sold them themselves and their children after he had taken possession of everything they owned, then he freed them and returned all their money to them, God knows best the truth of that, and it is from the Israelite stories that are neither true nor false, and the point is that he was among those who came to provide provisions from the brothers of Joseph on the orders of their father to them in that, for it reached them that the Aziz of Egypt gives people food in exchange for its price, so they took with them merchandise to exchange for food, and ten men rode, and Jacob, peace be upon him, kept his son Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, peace be upon him, with him, and he was the most beloved of his sons to him after Joseph, so when they entered upon Joseph while he was sitting in his splendor and leadership and sovereignty, he recognized them when he looked at them, and they did not know him, that is, they did not know him, because they left him when he was a young boy, and they sold him to the caravan and they did not know where to go with him, nor did they sense in themselves that he would become what he became, so for this reason they did not know him, but he recognized them. Al-Suddi and others mentioned that he began to address them, and said to them as if he was denouncing them: What brought you to my country? They said: O noble one, we have come to provide provisions. He said: Perhaps you are spies? They said: God forbid. He said: Where are you from? They said: From the land of Canaan, and our father Jacob is the prophet of God. He said: Does he have children other than you? They said: Yes, we were twelve, and the youngest of us went and perished in the wilderness, and he was the dearest of us to his father, and his brother remained, so his father kept him to entertain him, so he ordered that they be brought down and honored. And when he had furnished them with their provisions, meaning that he had given them their full measure and carried their loads, he said: “Bring me this brother of yours whom you mentioned so that I may know your truthfulness in what you have mentioned. “Do you not see that I give full measure, and I am the best of those who provide accommodations?” He encouraged them to return to him, then he frightened them and said: But if you do not bring him to me, you will have no measure with me, meaning that if you do not bring him with you the second time, you will have no provisions with me, and do not come near him. They said: We will surely entice his father away from him, and we will surely do so. That is, we will make every effort to bring him to you, and we will leave no stone unturned so that you may know our truthfulness in what we have said. Al-Suddi mentioned that he took hostages from them so that they would bring him with them, and there is consideration in this because he was kind to them and encouraged them greatly, and this was due to his eagerness for them to return. And he said to his young men, meaning His servants, Put their merchandise that is, what they brought to buy something in exchange for it in their baggage that is, in their luggage from where they do not notice, perhaps they will return with it. It was said: Joseph, peace be upon him, feared that they would not have other merchandise to return with for provisions. It was also said: He was reluctant to take something from his father and brothers in exchange for food. It was also said that he wanted to send them back if they found it in their luggage out of caution and piety, because he knew that from them, and God knows best.

Some of them read it with a ya', meaning he will measure, and indeed, we will guard him, meaning do not worry about him, for he will return to you. This is like what they said to him about Joseph, Send him with us tomorrow, that he may frolic and play, and indeed, we will guard him. For this reason, he said to them, Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother before? meaning, will you do with him except as you did with his brother before, keeping him away from me and standing between me and him? Then God is the best guardian, and some of them read it as guardian. And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, meaning He is the Most Merciful of the merciful to me, and He will have mercy on my old age, my weakness, and my sorrow over my son, and I hope that God will return him to me and reunite me with him, for He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.

12:66: God Almighty says: And when Joseph's brothers opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them, which was what Joseph had ordered his young men to put in their saddlebags. 12:67: God Almighty says, telling about Jacob, peace be upon him, that he ordered his sons when he prepared them with their brother Benjamin to go to Egypt not to all enter from one gate, but to enter from separate gates, because as Ibn Abbas, Muhammad bin Kaab, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, As-Suddi and more than one person said, he feared the evil eye for them, because they were beautiful and had a good appearance, and a splendid appearance, so he feared that people would strike them with their eyes, because the evil eye is real and can cause a rider to fall from his horse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i regarding his statement, And enter from separate gates, that he knew that he would meet his brothers at some of those gates. And His statement, And I cannot avail you at all against God, meaning that this precaution does not ward off God’s decree and judgment, for when God wills something, it cannot be opposed or prevented. “The judgment belongs only to God. Upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let the reliant rely.” And when they entered from where their father had commanded them, it could not avail them at all against God, except a need in Jacob’s soul which He fulfilled. They said: It was to ward off the evil eye from them. And indeed, he was full of knowledge because of what We taught him. Qatadah and Ath-Thawri said: He acted upon his knowledge. Ibn Jarir said: He was full of knowledge because of our teaching him, but most of the people do not know.

12:70: When he had prepared them and loaded their camels with food, he ordered some of his young men to place the siqaya, which is a silver vessel according to most, and it was said: of gold, Ibn Zayd said, he used to drink from it, and measure people with it because food was scarce at that time, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said, and Shu`bah said on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: the king’s cup, he said: it was made of silver and they used to drink from it, and it was like a shuttle, and Abbas had something similar in the pre-Islamic period, so he placed it in Benjamin’s belongings so that no one would notice, then a crier called out among them, O caravan, you are thieves, so they turned to the crier and said, What are you missing? * They said, we are missing the king’s cup, meaning his cup with which he measures, and whoever brings it will have a camel load, and this is from the category of reward, and I will be responsible for it, and this is from the category of guarantee and surety.

12:73: When those young men accused them of stealing, Joseph's brothers said to them, By God, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, nor were we thieves. That is, you have realized and known since you knew us, because they saw good conduct from them. We did not come to cause corruption in the land, nor were we thieves. That is, our natures do not require this characteristic. So the young men said to them, Then what is his penalty? That is, the thief, if he is among you, if you are liars. That is, what will be his punishment if we find among you someone who took him? “They said, ‘His recompense is he in whose saddlebag it is found. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.’” This was the law of Abraham, peace be upon him, that the thief should return it to the one from whom it was stolen. This is what Joseph, peace be upon him, wanted. For this reason, he began with their vessels before his brother’s vessel, meaning that he searched them before him as a euphemism. Then he extracted it from his brother’s vessel. So he took it from them based on their confession and commitment, and obligating them to what they believed. For this reason, God Almighty said, Thus did We plan for Joseph. This is from the beloved and intended plot that God loves and is pleased with, because of the wisdom and desired benefit in it. And his saying: He would not have taken his brother in the religion of the king meaning he would not have taken him in the rule of the king of Egypt, as Ad-Dahhak and others said. Rather, God decreed for him that his brothers committed to him what they committed to, and he knew that from their law, and for this reason God the Most High praised him and said: We raise by degrees whom We will as God the Most High said: God will raise those who believe among you Al-Basri 1:17, And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: There is no scholar except that there is another scholar above him until he reaches God the Almighty, and thus Abd Al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Abd Al-A’la Al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, who said: As with Ibn Abbas, so he told a strange hadith, and a man was amazed and said: Praise be to God, above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing, so Ibn Abbas said: What you said is bad: God the All-Knowing is above every scholar, and thus Samak narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing he said: This one is more knowledgeable than this one, and this one is more knowledgeable than this one, and God is above every scholar, and thus Ikrimah said, and Qatada said: And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is All-Knowing. All-Knowing, All-Wise, until knowledge ends with God, from Him it began, and the scholars learned, and to Him it returns, and in the reading of Abdullah, and above every scholar is the All-Knowing.

12:77: And Joseph's brothers said when they saw the cup taken out of Benjamin's belongings, If he steals, a brother of his stole before. They were disavowing the Aziz from imitating him, and they mentioned that this act was like a brother of his had done before, meaning Joseph, peace be upon him. Saeed bin Jubair said, on the authority of Qatada: Joseph, peace be upon him, had stolen an idol belonging to his maternal grandfather and broken it. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The first affliction that befell Joseph, as I have heard, was that his aunt, the daughter of Isaac, was the eldest son of Isaac, and she had Isaac’s belt, and they used to inherit it through old age. So whoever hid it from those who were in charge of it had a safe haven that was not disputed, and he could do with it as he wished. When Joseph was born to Jacob, his aunt had taken him into her care, and he was hers and his, and she did not love anyone as she loved him until he grew up and reached the age of years. Jacob’s soul, peace be upon him, yearned for him, so he came to her and said: O my sister, hand Joseph over to me, for by God I cannot bear for him to be absent from me for an hour. She said: By God, I will not leave him. Then she said: Leave him with me for a few days so that I may look at him and calm down, perhaps that will console me about him, or something like that. When Jacob left her, she went to Isaac’s belt and tied it around Joseph from under his clothes. Then she said: I lost the belt of Isaac, peace be upon him. See who took it and who took it? So she looked, then she said: Search the people of the house. They searched them and found it with Joseph. She said: By God, it is mine, and I can do with it as I wish. So Jacob came to him and she told him the story. He said to her: You and that. If he did that, then it is yours. I cannot do anything else. So she held him back, but Jacob could not do anything to him until she died. He said: He is the one who Joseph’s brothers said when he did to his brother what he did when he captured him: If he steals, a brother of his stole before. And his saying: So Joseph kept it to himself means the word that comes after it, which is his saying: You are in the worst place, and God knows best what you describe, meaning what you mention. He said this to himself and did not reveal it to them, and this is from the category of concealment before mention, and it is common, like the saying of the poet: His sons rewarded Abu Al-Ghailan for his greatness and good deeds, just as they reward Sinmar. There are many examples of this in the Qur’an, Hadith, and language in its prose, report, and poetry. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So Joseph kept it to himself, meaning he kept it to himself, You are in the worst position, and God knows best what you describe.
12:78: When it was necessary to take Benjamin and it was decided to leave him with Joseph according to their confession, they began to be kind to him and to show him compassion towards them. “They said, ‘O noble one, indeed he has an old father. ’” They meant that he loved him intensely and was comforted by him for his lost son. Take one of us in his place. That is, replace him and he will be with you as a substitute for him. Indeed, we see that you are among the doers of good. That is, the just, fair-minded, and receptive to good. “He said, ‘God forbid that we should take except him with whom we found our property. ’” That is, as you said and confessed. Indeed, then we would be wrongdoers. That is, if we took an innocent person who was sick.

12:80: God Almighty tells about Joseph's brothers that when they despaired of freeing their brother Benjamin, whom they had pledged to their father to return to him, and had made a covenant with him to do so, but that was prevented from them, they secreted, that is, they separated themselves from the people in secret, whispering among themselves. Their eldest said, who was Reuben, and it was said: Judah, and he was the one who advised them to throw him in the well when they intended to kill him, he said to them: Did you not know that your father took a covenant from you from God to return him to him? You have seen how that was difficult for you with what you had previously done of losing Joseph from him. I will not leave the land, that is, I will not leave this town until my father gives me permission to return to him, pleased with me, or God judges for me, it was said: by the sword, and it was said: by enabling me to take my brother and He is the best of judges. Then He ordered them to tell their father the manner of what had happened, so that it would be an excuse for them before him, and they would renounce to him and be innocent of what had happened by saying and His saying: And we were not guardians of the unseen. Qatada and Ikrimah said: We did not know that your son had stolen. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: We did not know of the unseen that anything had been stolen from him. We only asked: What is the punishment for a thief? And ask the town in which we were: It was said that what was meant was Egypt, as Qatada said, and it was said that it was another one. And the caravan in which we came meaning the one we accompanied, about our truthfulness, honesty, preservation and guarding, and indeed, we are truthful in what we told you about him stealing and they took him for his theft.

12:83: He said to them as he said to them when they came upon Joseph's shirt with false blood: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so have patience is most fitting. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When they came to Jacob and told him what had happened, he accused them and thought it was like what they had done to Joseph. He said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so have patience is most fitting. Some people said: Since their action was based on their first action, the ruling of the first was applied to him, and his statement was correct: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so have patience is most fitting. Then he hoped that God would return to him his three sons: Joseph, his brother Benjamin, and Reuben, who had stayed in Egypt awaiting God's command concerning him, either that his father would be pleased with him and order him to return to him, or that he would take his brother secretly. For this reason he said: "Perhaps God will bring them all to me. Indeed, He is the Knowing," meaning the Knowing of my condition, the Wise in His actions, judgment, and destiny. And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my grief over Joseph,' meaning he turned away from them. Son, he said, remembering the old grief of Joseph, Oh, my sorrow for Joseph! It is said that he lifted the crown from his forehead, where there was a mole, and said, Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant? meaning how they separated him from his brother, when you were ignorant? meaning that what made you do this was due to the extent of what you had committed, as some of the predecessors said: Everyone who disobeyed God is ignorant, and he recited, Then your Lord is for those who did evil in ignorance, the verse, and it appears - and God knows best - that Joseph, peace be upon him, only recognized himself to them with God Almighty’s permission for him to do so, just as he only hid himself from them both times. The first to do so were those who were ordered by God the Almighty, and God knows best. But when the situation became difficult and the matter became severe, God the Almighty relieved them of that difficulty, as He the Almighty said: “For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.” At that point, they said, Are you indeed Joseph? Ubayy ibn Ka’b read, Are you indeed Joseph? Ibn Muhaisin read, You are Joseph. The famous reading is the first, because the question indicates astonishment, meaning that they were amazed by that, that they had been visiting him for two years or more without knowing him, and yet he knew them and concealed himself from them. For this reason, they said, by way of question, Are you indeed Joseph? He said, I am Joseph, and this is my brother. And His saying: God has bestowed His favor upon us meaning by bringing us together after separation and after a period of time “Indeed, whoever fears God and is patient, then indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good. They said: By God, God has favored you over us” the verse, they say, acknowledging His favor and preference over them in creation, character, spaciousness, kingship, control, and prophethood as well, according to the saying of those who did not make them prophets, and they acknowledged to Him that they had wronged him and sinned against him “He said: There is no blame upon you today” meaning: There is no reprimand upon you or reproach upon you today, and I will not repeat your sin against me after today, then He increased their supplication for their forgiveness and said: God will forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Al-Suddi said: They apologized to Joseph, so he said: There is no blame upon you today meaning: I will not mention your sin to you. Ibn Ishaq and Al-Thawri said: There is no blame upon you meaning: There is no reprimand upon you today in My presence for what you did, God will forgive you meaning: God will cover what you did and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel informed us on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi al-Hudhayl, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: And when the caravan departed, he said: When the caravan departed, a wind blew, and it brought Jacob the scent of Joseph's shirt, so he said: Indeed, I smell the fragrance of Joseph, unless you think you are ignorant, he said: So he found his scent from a distance of eight days, and Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and others narrated it on the authority of Abu Sinan with it. Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said: There were eighty farsakhs between them, and it was between him and him since they parted. Eighty years. And his saying, Had you not been refuted, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Qatadah, and Saeed bin Jubair said, You are foolish. And Mujahid also said, and Al-Hasan said, You are becoming old. And their saying, Indeed, you are in your old error, Ibn Abbas said, Indeed, in your old mistake. Qatadah said, That is, from the love of Joseph, you do not forget him or console yourself with him. They said a harsh word to their father that they should not have said to their father or to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Al-Suddi and others said the same.

12:96: Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Al-Basheer means the messenger. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: It was Judah bin Ya'qub. As-Suddi said: He only brought it because he was the one who brought the shirt stained with false blood, so he wanted to wash it with this, so he brought the shirt and threw it on his father's face and he regained his sight. Then he said to his sons: Did I not tell you that I know from God that which you do not know? That is, I know that God will return him to me. And I said to you: Indeed, I smell the fragrance of Joseph, unless you think it is false. Then they said to their father, being gentle with him: "O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins. Indeed, we were sinners. He said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who repents to Him, He will accept his repentance." Ibn Mas'ud, Ibrahim At-Taymi, Amr bin Qais, Ibn Jurayj and others said: He postponed them until the time of dawn. Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa’ib told me, Ibn Idris told us, I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq mentioning on the authority of Muharib ibn Dithar who said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to come to the mosque and hear a man saying: O God, You called upon me and I answered, You commanded me and I obeyed, and this is the last part of the night, so forgive me. He said: So he listened to the voice, and it was from the house of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, so he asked Abdullah about that, and he said: Indeed, Jacob delayed his sons until the last part of the night by saying: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. It was mentioned in the hadith that this was on Friday night, as Ibn Jarir also said: Al-Muthanna told me, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman Ayyub al-Dimashqi told us, al-Walid told us, Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Ata’ and Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, meaning: until Friday night comes, and it is the saying of the brother of Jacob to his sons. This is strange from this perspective, and there is a problem with its being attributed to the Prophet, and God knows best.

12:99: God Almighty tells about the arrival of Jacob, peace be upon him, to Joseph, peace be upon him, and his arrival in the land of Egypt, when Joseph had asked his brothers to bring him all their families, so they all carried them, and departed from the land of Canaan heading to the land of Egypt, so when Joseph, peace be upon him, was informed of their approach, he went out to meet them and the king ordered his princes and the most prominent people to go out with Joseph to meet the Prophet of God, Jacob, peace be upon him, and it is said: The king also went out to meet him, and this is more likely, and his statement: He took his parents into his care and said, 'Enter Egypt,' has been confusing to many commentators, so some of them said: This is from the introduction and the delay, and the meaning of the statement is And he said, 'Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety' and he took his parents into his care and raised them to the throne, and Ibn Jarir rejected this, and he did well in that, then he chose what he narrated from Al-Suddi that Joseph took his parents into his care when he met them, then when they reached the gate of the city he said: Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety and there is also a consideration in this, because the shelter is only It is in the house, as he said, He took his brother into his home, and in the hadith, He who takes in an innovator. What prevents him from saying to them after they entered upon him and he took them into his home: Enter Egypt, and he included in it, Reside in Egypt, God willing, in safety, meaning from the hardship and famine you were in. It is said - and God knows best - that God Almighty lifted from the people of Egypt the rest of the barren years by the blessing of Jacob’s arrival upon them, just as He lifted the rest of the years that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for against the people of Mecca when he said, O God, help me against them with seven like the seven of Joseph. Then when they supplicated to him and sought intercession with him, and sent Abu Sufyan in that, he prayed for them and lifted the rest of that from them by the blessing of his prayer, peace be upon him. And his saying: And he took his parents to him Al-Suddi and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was his father and his maternal aunt, and his mother had died long ago. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir said: His father and mother were alive. Ibn Jarir said: There is no evidence that his mother died, and the apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that she was alive, and this is the one who supported him, the victorious one, as indicated by the context. And his saying: And he raised his parents upon the throne Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: It means the bed, i.e. he seated them with him on his bed, and they fell down before him in prostration i.e. his parents and the rest of his brothers prostrated before him. They were eleven men, and he said, O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of old, meaning the one he had told his father before, Indeed, I saw eleven stars, the verse. This was permissible in their laws, if they greeted the elder, they would prostrate to him, and this remained permissible from the time of Adam until the law of Jesus, peace be upon him, then this was forbidden in this religion, and prostration was made specific to the side of the Lord, glory be to Him, the Most High. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada and others. It is narrated in the hadith that Muadh came to Ash-Sham and found them prostrating to their bishops. When he returned, he prostrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, What is this, O Muadh? He said, I saw them prostrating to their bishops, and you are more deserving of being prostrated to, O Messenger of God. He said, If I were to command anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would have commanded the woman to prostrate to her husband because of the great right he has over her. In another hadith: Salman met the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on one of the streets of Medina. Salman was a new convert to Islam, so he prostrated to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Do not prostrate to me, O Salman, but prostrate to the Ever-Living One who does not die. The point is that this was permissible in their law, and for this reason they prostrated to him. Then Joseph said: “O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true.” That is, this is what the matter has come to, for interpretation is applied to what a matter will come to, as God Almighty said: Do they await anything but its interpretation? The Day its interpretation comes? That is, on the Day of Resurrection, what they were promised of good and evil will come to them. And his saying: My Lord has made it true meaning, it is true and true, mentioning the blessings of God upon him, And He was kind to me when He brought me out of prison and brought you from the desert meaning, the desert. Ibn Jurayj and others said: They were people of the desert and livestock, and he said: They lived in the Arabs in the land of Palestine from the Ghor of Ash-Sham, and he said: And some say: They were in Al-Awlaj from the direction of a valley lower than Hisma, and they were people of the desert and sheep and camels, “After Satan had sown dissension between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle to whom He wills” meaning, if He wills a matter, He provides for it the means and decrees it and makes it easy. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing of the interests of His servants, the Wise in His words and actions and His judgment and decree and what He chooses and wills. Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi said, on the authority of Sulayman: There were forty years between Joseph’s vision and its interpretation. Abdullah bin Shaddad said: And this is where the farthest point of the vision ends. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. He also said: Umar bin Ali told us, Abdul Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It was eighty years from the time Joseph left Jacob until they met. Sorrow never left his heart, and his tears ran down his cheeks. There was no servant on the face of the earth more beloved to God than Jacob. Hisham said, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Eighty-three years. Mubarak bin Fadala said, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, so he was absent from his father for eighty years. He lived after that for twenty-three years, then he died at the age of one hundred and twenty years. Qatada said: There were thirty-five years between them. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: It was mentioned - and God knows best - that Joseph's absence from Jacob was eighteen years. He said: The People of the Book claim that it was forty years or so, and that Jacob, peace be upon him, remained with Joseph after he came to him in Egypt for seventeen years, then God took him to Himself. Abu Ishaq Al-Subai'i said, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, who said: The Children of Israel entered Egypt and they were sixty-three people, and they left it with six hundred and seventy thousand. Abu Ishaq said, on the authority of Masruq: They entered and they were three hundred and ninety, between men and women. And God knows best. Musa bin Ubaidah said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad: The family of Jacob gathered with Joseph in Egypt, and they were eighty-six al-Nas 114:young and old, male and female, and they left it, and they were more than six hundred thousand.
