Abdullah bin Shaddad said: And this is where the farthest point of the vision ends. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. He also said: Umar bin Ali told us, Abdul Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It was eighty years from the time Joseph left Jacob until they met. Sorrow never left his heart, and his tears ran down his cheeks. There was no servant on the face of the earth more beloved to God than Jacob. Hisham said, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Eighty-three years. Mubarak bin Fadala said, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, so he was absent from his father for eighty years. He lived after that for twenty-three years, then he died at the age of one hundred and twenty years. Qatada said: There were thirty-five years between them. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: It was mentioned - and God knows best - that Joseph's absence from Jacob was eighteen years. He said: The People of the Book claim that it was forty years or so, and that Jacob, peace be upon him, remained with Joseph after he came to him in Egypt for seventeen years, then God took him to Himself. Abu Ishaq Al-Subai'i said, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, who said: The Children of Israel entered Egypt and they were sixty-three people, and they left it with six hundred and seventy thousand. Abu Ishaq said, on the authority of Masruq: They entered and they were three hundred and ninety, between men and women. And God knows best. Musa bin Ubaidah said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad: The family of Jacob gathered with Joseph in Egypt, and they were eighty-six al-Nas 114:young and old, male and female, and they left it, and they were more than six hundred thousand.
12:101: This is a supplication from Joseph the Truthful, he supplicated to his Lord Almighty with it when God's blessing was completed upon him by his meeting with his parents and brothers, and what God bestowed upon him of prophethood and kingship. He asked his Lord Almighty, just as He completed His blessing upon him in this world, to continue it upon him in the hereafter, and to cause him to die as a Muslim when he dies. Ad-Dahhak said: And to join him with the righteous, who are his brothers from the prophets and messengers, may God's prayers and peace be upon them all. This supplication may have been said by Joseph, peace be upon him, when it was abbreviated, as was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, would raise his finger when dying and say: O God, in the highest company three times. It may also be that he asked to die as a Muslim and to join the righteous when his time came and his life ended, not that he asked Him to fulfill it as the supplicant says to another: May God cause you to die as a Muslim, and the supplicant says: O God, let us live as Muslims, and cause us to die as Muslims, and join us with the righteous. It is possible that he asked for that in full, and that was permissible in their religion, as Qatada said regarding his statement: Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous, when God gathered his affairs and comforted his eyes, and he was on that day immersed in the world, its kingdom and its freshness, and he longed for the righteous before him. Ibn Abbas used to say: No prophet ever wished for death before Joseph, peace be upon him. Ibn Jarir and Al-Suddi also mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was the first prophet to pray for that. This means that he was the first to ask for death in Islam, just as Noah was the first to say: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer. It is also possible that he was the first to ask for that to be fulfilled, and this is the apparent context of Qatada’s statement, but this is not permissible in our Sharia. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim told us, Abdul Aziz ibn Suhaib told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Let none of you wish for death because of a calamity that has befallen him. If he must wish for death, then let him say: O God, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and take me if death is good for me.” And they included it in the two Sahihs, and they have it: “Let none of you wish for death because of a calamity that has befallen him, either he is a good person, so he increases his good deeds, or he is a bad person, so perhaps he will repent. But let him say: O God, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and take me if death is good for me.” Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Ma’an bin Rafa’ah told us, Ali bin Yazid told me on the authority of Al-Qasim on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: We sat with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we mentioned and felt tenderness, and Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas cried and cried a lot, and said: I wish I were dead. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Sa’d, do you wish for death with me? He repeated that three times, then he said: O Sa`d, if you were created for Paradise, then the longer your life and the better your deeds are, the better for you. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi`ah told us, Abu Yunus told us, and he is Salim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Let none of you wish for death because of a calamity that has befallen him, nor supplicate for it before it befalls him, unless he is confident in his deeds, for when one of you dies, his life is cut short, and nothing increases the life of the believer except good.” Ahmad alone reported it. This is if the calamity is specific to him. However, if it is a trial in religion, then it is permissible to ask for death, as God Almighty said, informing about the magicians when Pharaoh wanted them to abandon their religion and threatened them with death: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and let us die as Muslims. And Mary said, when the labor pains came to her, that is, the contractions, to the trunk of the palm tree: Oh, I wish I had died before this and was forgotten. This is because she knew that people were accusing her of immorality, because she did not have a husband, and she had become pregnant and given birth. They said: “O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented. O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.” So God made a way out and a way out for her from that state, and made the child speak in the cradle that he was the servant of God and His Messenger. So it was a great sign and a dazzling miracle, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him. And in the hadith of Muadh, which was narrated by Imam Ahmad and Al-Tirmidhi in the story of the dream and the supplication in which it says, And if you intend for a people a trial, then take me to You before I am tested. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Salamah told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Asim bin Omar bin Qatada, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Labid, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are two things that the son of Adam hates: he hates death, and death is better for the believer than trials, and he hates lack of wealth, and lack of wealth means less accountability.” So when trials occur in religion, it is permissible to ask for death. For this reason, Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said at the end of his caliphate when he saw that things were not going well for him and that things were only getting worse, so he said: O God, take me to You, for I am tired of them and they are tired of me. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said: When that trial happened to him and what happened to him with the Emir of Khurasan happened, he said: O God, take me to You. And in the hadith: “A man passes by a grave - meaning in the time of the Antichrist - and says: I wish I were in your place,” because of what he sees of trials, earthquakes, troubles, and terrible things that are a trial for every tempted person. Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: It was mentioned that the sons of Jacob who did to Joseph what they did, their father asked forgiveness for them, so God repented to them, forgave them, and pardoned their sins. Mention who said that Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Salih Al-Mari, on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: When God, the Most High, gathered his family together with his two eyes, He left his sons alone, and some of them said to one another: Do you not know what you have done? And what the old man suffered from you, and what Joseph suffered from you? They said: Yes. He said: So their forgiveness of you deceives you, so what will you do with your Lord? So their affair was settled so that they went to the old man, and they sat before him, and Joseph was sitting beside his father. They said: O our father, we have come to you for a matter like which we have never come to you for before, and a matter has befallen us like which has never befallen us before, until they stirred it up, and the prophets, peace be upon them, are the most merciful of creation. He said: What is the matter with you, my sons? They said: Do you not know what happened from us to you and what happened from us to our brother Joseph? He said: Yes. They said: Have you not forgiven us? They said: Yes. They said: Your forgiveness will not avail us at all, if God has not forgiven us. He said: What do you want, my sons? They said: We want you to pray to God for us, so that when the revelation comes to you from God that He has forgiven us, our eyes will be comforted and our hearts will be reassured, otherwise we will never have comfort in this world. He said: So the old man stood up and faced the qiblah and Yusuf stood behind his father, and they stood behind them, humbled and submissive. He said: So he prayed and Yusuf responded, but they did not answer for twenty years. Salih al-Murri said: He was frightening them. He said: Until when he was on the verge of twenty, Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended upon Jacob, peace be upon him, and said: God the Almighty has sent me to you to give you good report that He has answered your prayer regarding your son and that God the Almighty has forgiven what they did, and that He has fulfilled their covenants after you regarding prophethood. This narration is attributed to Anas. Yazid al-Raqashi and Salih al-Murri are very weak. Al-Suddi mentioned that when death approached Jacob, peace be upon him, he recommended to Joseph that he be buried near Abraham and Isaac, so when he died, he was patient and sent him to Syria, and he was buried near them, peace be upon them.
12:102: God Almighty says to Muhammad, peace be upon him, when he told him the story of Joseph's brothers, and how God raised him up over them, and made for him the end, victory, kingship and rule, despite what they intended for him of evil, destruction and execution, this and similar things, O Muhammad, from the previous report of the unseen, We reveal it to you and we inform you of it, O Muhammad, because it contains a lesson for you, and a warning for those who oppose you, and you were not with them present with them nor watching them when they decided their plan that is, to throw him into the well and they were plotting against him, but We informed you of it as a revelation to you and a revelation to you, like His saying: And you were not with them when they cast their pens verse, and God Almighty said: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Moses verse, until His saying: And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called verse, and He said: And you were not residing among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses verse, and He said: I had no knowledge of the highest assembly when they disputed. * It is not revealed to me except that I am a clear warner. God Almighty says: He is His Messenger and He has informed him of the report of what had come before, which contains a lesson for people and salvation for them in their religion and their worldly life. Despite this, most people did not believe, and for this reason He said: And most people are not believers, even if you were eager to do so. And He said: And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will mislead you from the way of God. Like His statement: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers. And His statement: And you do not ask them for any reward for it. That is, you do not ask them, O Muhammad, for this advice and call to goodness and guidance for any reward, that is, any reward or wage for that, rather you do it seeking the face of God and advising His creation. It is only a reminder for the worlds. They remember by it and are guided and saved by it in this world and the hereafter.

12:105: The Almighty tells us about the heedlessness of most people in contemplating the signs of God and the evidence of His Oneness, with what God has created in the heavens and the earth of shining fixed planets, and planets and revolving orbits, all of which are subject to Him. How many adjacent pieces are there on the earth, and gardens and paradises, and steadfast mountains, and abundant seas, and turbulent waves, and vast deserts, and how many living and dead people, and animals and plants, and fruits similar and different in tastes, smells, colors and qualities, so glory be to the One, the Unique, Creator of all kinds of creatures, the One who is unique in perpetuity, survival and self-sufficiency of names and qualities, and other than that. And His statement: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. Ibn Abbas said: Part of their faith is that when it is said to them: Who created the heavens, and who created the earth, and who created the mountains? They say: God, while they associate others with Him. And this is what Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Ash-Sha’bi, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. And in the two Sahihs: That the polytheists used to say in their Talbiyah: Here I am, you have no partner except a partner who is yours, you own him and what he owns. And in Sahih Muslim it is mentioned that when they said: Here I am, you have no partner, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say: Qad qad meaning enough, enough, do not say more than this. And God the Most High said: Indeed, associating others with God is a great wrong. And this is the greatest polytheism, worshipping someone other than God, as in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. I said: O Messenger of God, which sin is the greatest? He said: To make a rival to God even though He created you. Al-Hasan al-Basri said about his statement: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. He said: That hypocrite acts when he acts to show off to people, and he is a polytheist by his action. He means the statement of God the Almighty: “Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but it is He who deceives them. And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering God except a little.” And there is another hidden polytheism that its doer is usually not aware of, as Hammad ibn Salamah narrated on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud on the authority of Urwah, who said: Hudhayfah entered upon a sick person and saw a belt on his arm, so he cut it off - or pulled it out - and then said: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. And in the hadith: Whoever swears by other than God has committed polytheism. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and he authenticated it from the narration of Ibn Umar. And in the hadith that Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Saud, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, incantations, amulets and love charms are polytheism. And in a wording of theirs: Superstition is polytheism, and there is none of us who does not, but God removes it through reliance. And it was narrated by Imam Ahmad said more simply than this: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Yahya Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Zainab’s nephew, on the authority of Zainab, the wife of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: When Abdullah came to the door to do something he needed, he would clear his throat and spit, not wanting to attack us with something he disliked. She said: One day he came and cleared his throat, and I had an old woman with me to treat me with a cold sore, so I brought her under the bed. She said: He came in and sat next to me, and he saw a string around my neck, so he said: What is this string? She said: I said: A string of incantation for me, so he took it and cut it and then said: The family of Abdullah are rich and do not need polytheism. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Incantations, amulets and charms are polytheism. She said: I said to him: Why did you say that when my eyes were squinting, and I used to go to so-and-so the Jew to incantate over them, and when he incantated over them they would calm down, so he said: That is from the devil, he was prodding them with his hand, and when he incantated over them he would stop. It would have been sufficient for you to say as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Remove the affliction, O Lord of mankind, heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind.” In another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Isa bin Abdul Rahman, he said: I visited Abdullah bin Ukaim while he was sick, and he was asked: Why don’t you hang on to something? He said: Why don’t you hang on to something when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever hangs on to something will be entrusted to it. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever hangs on an amulet has committed shirk. And in another narration: “Whoever hangs on an amulet, may God not complete his affairs, and whoever hangs on a charm, may God not grant him peace.” And on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God said: I am the most independent of partners from shirk. Whoever does an action and associates someone with Me in it, I will leave him and his partner.” Narrated by Muslim. On the authority of Abu Saeed bin Abi Fadalah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When God gathers the first and the last on a Day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: ‘Whoever associated others with God in a deed he did for the sake of God, let him seek his reward from other than God, for God is the One Who has no need of partners.’” Narrated by Imam Ahmad. Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Yazid, meaning Ibn al-Hadi, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is minor polytheism. They said: What is minor polytheism, O Messenger of God? He said: “Showing off. God the Most High will say on the Day of Resurrection when He rewards people for their deeds: ‘Go to those for whom you showed off in the world and see if you find any reward with them.’” Ismail bin Ja’far narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, the freed slave of al-Muttalib, on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatadah, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, with the same chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Ibn Hubayrah told us, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is prevented from his need by superstition has committed shirk. They said: O Messenger of God, what is the expiation for that? He said: “That one of them should say: O God, there is no good except Your good, and no omen except Your omen, and there is no god but You.” Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numair told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulaiman Al-Arzami told us on the authority of Abu Ali - a man from Bani Kahil - who said: Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, beware of this polytheism, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Abdullah bin Hazn and Qais bin Al-Mudharib stood up and said: By God, you must either leave what you said, or we will come to Umar with or without permission. He said: Rather leave what you said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us one day and said: O people, beware of this polytheism, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Then whoever God willed to say it said to him: How can we beware of it when it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant, O Messenger of God? He said: Say: O God, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we ask Your forgiveness for what we do not know. It was narrated from another source, and in it that the questioner in that is the friend, as narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili from the hadith of Abdul Aziz bin Muslim, from Laith bin Abi Salim, from Abu Muhammad, from Muqal bin Yasar, who said: I witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or he said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq told me, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Polytheism is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant. Abu Bakr said: Is polytheism anything other than calling upon another god with God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Polytheism is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant. Then he said: “Shall I not guide you to something that will remove from you both the small and the great of that? Say: O God, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You while I know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Shaiban ibn Farukh, on the authority of Yahya ibn Katheer, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Polytheism is more hidden among my nation than the crawling of an ant on a rock. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, how is salvation and a way out of it? He said: Shall I not tell you of something that, if you say it, you will be absolved of its little or much, its small or great? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: “Say: O God, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You while I know, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know.” Ad-Daraqutni said: This Yahya ibn Katheer, who is called Abu An-Nadr, is an abandoned hadith narrator. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it and An-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Ya’la ibn Ata’, I heard Amr ibn Asim, I heard Abu Hurairah say: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, teach me something to say when I wake up and when I go to bed, he said: “Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord of everything and its King, I bear witness that there is no god but You, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of Satan and his polytheism.” Narrated by Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i who authenticated it, and Imam Ahmad added in his narration: From the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym from Mujahid, from Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) commanded me to say - and he mentioned this supplication and added at the end of it - and that I commit an evil against myself or cause it to be directed to a Muslim. And His statement: Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God verse, meaning, do these polytheists feel secure that a matter will come upon them that will overwhelm them from where they do not perceive, as God the Almighty said: “Do those who plot evil deeds then feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will seize them in their turning (about [astray], so they will not escape. Or that He will seize them while they are in fear? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.” And His statement: “Do the people of the towns then feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them at night while they are asleep? Or do the people of the towns then feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them at noon while they are playing? Do they then feel secure against the plan of God? But none feels secure from the plan of God except the losing people.”

They say: God, while they associate others with Him. And this is what Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Ash-Sha’bi, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. And in the two Sahihs: That the polytheists used to say in their Talbiyah: Here I am, you have no partner except a partner who is yours, you own him and what he owns. And in Sahih Muslim it is mentioned that when they said: Here I am, you have no partner, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would say: Qad qad meaning enough, enough, do not say more than this. And God the Most High said: Indeed, associating others with God is a great wrong. And this is the greatest polytheism, worshipping someone other than God, as in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud. I said: O Messenger of God, which sin is the greatest? He said: To make a rival to God even though He created you. Al-Hasan al-Basri said about his statement: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. He said: That hypocrite acts when he acts to show off to people, and he is a polytheist by his action. He means the statement of God the Almighty: “Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but it is He who deceives them. And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering God except a little.” And there is another hidden polytheism that its doer is usually not aware of, as Hammad ibn Salamah narrated on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud on the authority of Urwah, who said: Hudhayfah entered upon a sick person and saw a belt on his arm, so he cut it off - or pulled it out - and then said: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. And in the hadith: Whoever swears by other than God has committed polytheism. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and he authenticated it from the narration of Ibn Umar. And in the hadith that Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Saud, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, incantations, amulets and love charms are polytheism. And in a wording of theirs: Superstition is polytheism, and there is none of us who does not, but God removes it through reliance. And it was narrated by Imam Ahmad said more simply than this: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Yahya Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Zainab’s nephew, on the authority of Zainab, the wife of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: When Abdullah came to the door to do something he needed, he would clear his throat and spit, not wanting to attack us with something he disliked. She said: One day he came and cleared his throat, and I had an old woman with me to treat me with a cold sore, so I brought her under the bed. She said: He came in and sat next to me, and he saw a string around my neck, so he said: What is this string? She said: I said: A string of incantation for me, so he took it and cut it and then said: The family of Abdullah are rich and do not need polytheism. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Incantations, amulets and charms are polytheism. She said: I said to him: Why did you say that when my eyes were squinting, and I used to go to so-and-so the Jew to incantate over them, and when he incantated over them they would calm down, so he said: That is from the devil, he was prodding them with his hand, and when he incantated over them he would stop. It would have been sufficient for you to say as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Remove the affliction, O Lord of mankind, heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind.” In another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Isa bin Abdul Rahman, he said: I visited Abdullah bin Ukaim while he was sick, and he was asked: Why don’t you hang on to something? He said: Why don’t you hang on to something when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever hangs on to something will be entrusted to it. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever hangs on an amulet has committed shirk. And in another narration: “Whoever hangs on an amulet, may God not complete his affairs, and whoever hangs on a charm, may God not grant him peace.” And on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God said: I am the most independent of partners from shirk. Whoever does an action and associates someone with Me in it, I will leave him and his partner.” Narrated by Muslim. On the authority of Abu Saeed bin Abi Fadalah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When God gathers the first and the last on a Day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: ‘Whoever associated others with God in a deed he did for the sake of God, let him seek his reward from other than God, for God is the One Who has no need of partners.’” Narrated by Imam Ahmad. Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Yazid, meaning Ibn al-Hadi, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is minor polytheism. They said: What is minor polytheism, O Messenger of God? He said: “Showing off. God the Most High will say on the Day of Resurrection when He rewards people for their deeds: ‘Go to those for whom you showed off in the world and see if you find any reward with them.’” Ismail bin Ja’far narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, the freed slave of al-Muttalib, on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatadah, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, with the same chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Ibn Hubayrah told us, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is prevented from his need by superstition has committed shirk. They said: O Messenger of God, what is the expiation for that? He said: “That one of them should say: O God, there is no good except Your good, and no omen except Your omen, and there is no god but You.” Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numair told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulaiman Al-Arzami told us on the authority of Abu Ali - a man from Bani Kahil - who said: Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, beware of this polytheism, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Abdullah bin Hazn and Qais bin Al-Mudharib stood up and said: By God, you must either leave what you said, or we will come to Umar with or without permission. He said: Rather leave what you said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us one day and said: O people, beware of this polytheism, for it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant. Then whoever God willed to say it said to him: How can we beware of it when it is more hidden than the crawling of an ant, O Messenger of God? He said: Say: O God, we seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and we ask Your forgiveness for what we do not know. It was narrated from another source, and in it that the questioner in that is the friend, as narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili from the hadith of Abdul Aziz bin Muslim, from Laith bin Abi Salim, from Abu Muhammad, from Muqal bin Yasar, who said: I witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or he said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq told me, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Polytheism is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant. Abu Bakr said: Is polytheism anything other than calling upon another god with God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Polytheism is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant. Then he said: “Shall I not guide you to something that will remove from you both the small and the great of that? Say: O God, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You while I know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Shaiban ibn Farukh, on the authority of Yahya ibn Katheer, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Polytheism is more hidden among my nation than the crawling of an ant on a rock. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, how is salvation and a way out of it? He said: Shall I not tell you of something that, if you say it, you will be absolved of its little or much, its small or great? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: “Say: O God, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You while I know, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know.” Ad-Daraqutni said: This Yahya ibn Katheer, who is called Abu An-Nadr, is an abandoned hadith narrator. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it and An-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Ya’la ibn Ata’, I heard Amr ibn Asim, I heard Abu Hurairah say: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, teach me something to say when I wake up and when I go to bed, he said: “Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord of everything and its King, I bear witness that there is no god but You, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of Satan and his polytheism.” Narrated by Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i who authenticated it, and Imam Ahmad added in his narration: From the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym from Mujahid, from Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) commanded me to say - and he mentioned this supplication and added at the end of it - and that I commit an evil against myself or cause it to be directed to a Muslim. And His statement: Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God verse, meaning, do these polytheists feel secure that a matter will come upon them that will overwhelm them from where they do not perceive, as God the Almighty said: “Do those who plot evil deeds then feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will seize them in their turning (about [astray], so they will not escape. Or that He will seize them while they are in fear? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.” And His statement: “Do the people of the towns then feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them at night while they are asleep? Or do the people of the towns then feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them at noon while they are playing? Do they then feel secure against the plan of God? But none feels secure from the plan of God except the losing people.”

And His statement: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. Ibn Abbas said: Part of their faith is that when it is said to them: Who created the heavens, and who created the earth, and who created the mountains? 12:108: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the two kinds of beings: mankind and jinn, commanding him to inform people that this is his way, his method, his way, and his Sunnah, which is the call to testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. He calls to God with it on the basis of insight, certainty, and proof. He and everyone who follows him calls to what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to on the basis of insight, certainty, and rational and legal proof. And His statement: And glory be to God means that God is far above having a partner, equal, peer, rival, son, parent, companion, minister, or advisor. Blessed, sanctified, transcendent, and exalted above all of that, “The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.”
12:109: The Almighty informs us that He only sent His messengers from men, not from women, and this is the opinion of the majority of scholars, as indicated by the context of this noble verse that God did not inspire a woman from the daughters of Adam with legislative inspiration. Some of them claimed that Sarah, the wife of Abraham and the mother of Moses, and Mary, the daughter of Imran, the mother of Jesus, were prophetesses, and they argued that the angels gave Sarah the good report of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob, and by His saying: And We inspired the mother of Moses, saying, 'Suckle him' verse, and by the angel coming to Mary and giving her the good report of Jesus, peace be upon him, and by His saying: "When the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow.'" This amount was granted to them, but it does not necessarily mean that they were prophetesses because of that. If the one who says that their prophethood is intended to honor them, then there is no doubt about that, and the discussion with him remains as to whether this is sufficient to join the ranks of prophethood on its own or not? What the Sunnis and the community are upon, and what Sheikh Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Ismail al-Ash'ari transmitted from them, is that there are no prophetesses among women, but rather there are female friends, as God Almighty said, informing us about the most honorable of them, Mary, daughter of Imran, where God Almighty said: “The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers passed away before him. And his mother was a friend. They both used to eat food.” So He described her in the most honorable of her positions as a friend. If she were a prophet, that would have been mentioned in a position of honor and respect, so she is a friend according to the text of the Qur’an. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And We did not send before you, except men 1:13, meaning they are not from the people of heaven as you said. This statement of Ibn Abbas is supported by the statement of God the Almighty: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets 1:13, and the statement of God the Almighty: “And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal. Then We fulfilled for them the promise and saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors.” 1:13. And the statement of God the Almighty: Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers’ 1:13. And his statement: Of the people of the towns 1:13, what is meant by the towns are the cities, not that they are from the people of the deserts who are the most rude of people in nature and morals. This is the well-known norm that the people of the cities are more delicate in nature and gentle than the people of the blacks, and the people of the countryside and the blacks are closer in condition to those who live in the deserts. For this reason God the Almighty said: The desert Arabs are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy 1:13. Qatada said regarding his statement: Of the people of the towns 1:13, because they are more knowledgeable and patient than the people of the cities. In another hadith, a Bedouin man presented a camel to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he kept giving him more and more until he was satisfied. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was thinking of not giving a gift except to a Qurayshi, Ansari, Thaqafi, or Dawsi. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Yahya bin Waththab, on the authority of a sheikh from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-A’mash said: He is Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm is better than the one who does not mix with them and is not patient with their harm. And His saying: Have they not traveled through the land means those who denied you, O Muhammad, on the earth and observed how was the end of those before them meaning of the nations who denied the messengers, how God destroyed them and the disbelievers like them, like His saying: Have they not traveled through the land and had hearts by which to reason the verse, so when they heard the report of that they would see that God had destroyed the disbelievers and saved the believers, and this was His way with His creation, and for this reason the Most High said: And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God meaning just as We saved the believers in this world, so We wrote for them salvation in the home of the Hereafter, and it is much better for them than this world, like His saying: “Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand * The Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the worst home” and He added the home to the hereafter, so He said: And the home of the Hereafter as it is said: the first prayer and the congregational mosque, and the first year, and the first evening, and Thursday. And the poet said: You praise Faqqas and criticize Abs. By God, your mother is from a hybrid. Even if the land of Abs could overpower you, you would know humiliation with certainty.
12:110: The Almighty mentions that His victory descends upon His messengers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all, when the situation is difficult and they are waiting for relief from God at the most needed times, as in His Almighty’s saying: And they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, ‘When is the victory of God?’ (Al-Baqarah 2:177). And in His saying: They denied, there are two readings, one of them with emphasis: They denied. And that is how Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used to read it. Al-Bukhari said: Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah bin Az-Zubayr told me, on the authority of Aisha, that she said to him while he was asking her about the saying of God Almighty: Until when the messengers despaired, he said: I said: Did they deny or did they lie? Aisha said: They lied. I said: They were certain that their people had denied them, so what is it by suspicion? She said: Yes, by my life, they were certain of that. I said to her: And they thought that they had been denied. She said: God forbid! The messengers would not have thought that about their Lord. I said: What is this verse? She said: They are the followers of the messengers who believed in their Lord and confirmed them, but the affliction was prolonged for them and victory was delayed from them until the messengers despaired of those among their people who had denied them, and the messengers thought that their followers had denied them, then the victory of God came. Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri who said: Urwah told us, so I said to her: Perhaps it is they were denied in the light form? She said: God forbid. End of what he mentioned. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abi Malekah told me that Ibn Abbas read it as and they thought that they had been denied lightly. Abdullah said: He is Ibn Abi Malekah. Then Ibn Abbas said to me: They were human beings. Then he recited: “Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say: When is the help of God? Unquestionably, the help of God is near.” Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abi Malekah told me, and Urwah told me on the authority of Aisha that she contradicted that and refused it, and said: God did not promise Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, anything except that He knew that it would happen until he died. However, the trials of the messengers continued until they thought that those who were with them from the believers had denied them. Ibn Abi Malekah said in the hadith of Urwah: Aisha used to read it as and they thought that they had been denied heavy from the denial. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Sulayman bin Bilal told me on the authority of Yahya bin Sa’id, who said: A man came to Al-Qasim bin Muhammad and said: Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi recited this verse: Until when the messengers gave up hope and thought that they were denied. Al-Qasim said: Tell him on my authority that I heard Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Until when the messengers gave up hope and thought that they were denied. She said: Their followers denied them. The chain of transmission is also sound. The second reading is with a light pronunciation, and they differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas said what was mentioned above. And on the authority of Ibn Masoud, in what Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, that he read Until when the messengers gave up hope and thought that they had been denied with a light pronunciation. Abdullah said: It is what you hate. This is on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with them, and it contradicts what others narrated on their authority. As for Ibn Abbas, al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Muslim on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Until when the messengers gave up hope and thought that they had been denied, he said: When the messengers gave up hope that their people would respond to them and their people thought that the messengers had denied them, victory came to them for that, And We saved whom We willed. And similarly it was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Imran bin al-Harith al-Sulami, Abd al-Rahman bin Muawiyah, Ali bin Abi Talhah, and al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a similar word. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Arim Abu Al-Nu’man told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Shu’aib told us, Ibrahim bin Abi Harrah Al-Jazari told us: A young man from Quraysh asked Saeed bin Jubayr and said to him: O Abu Abdullah, what is this letter, for when I come to it I wish that I had not read this surah Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied? He said: Yes, until the messengers despaired of their people believing them, and the ones to whom they were sent thought that the messengers had lied. Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: I have never seen a man called to knowledge who hesitates like today. If I traveled to Yemen for this, it would be little. Then Ibn Jarir also narrated from another source that Muslim ibn Yasar asked Saeed ibn Jubayr about that, and he answered him with this answer. So he went to Saeed and embraced him and said: May God relieve you as you relieved me. And it was narrated from more than one source from Saeed ibn Jubayr that he interpreted it in this way. And Mujahid ibn Jabr and more than one of the early Muslims interpreted it in this way, until Mujahid read it and they thought that they had lied with the opening of the dhal. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, except that some of those who interpreted it in this way return the pronoun in his statement and they thought that they had lied to the followers of the messengers from the believers, and some of them return it to the disbelievers among them, meaning that the disbelievers thought that the messengers had lied, lightening what they were promised of victory. As for Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Jahsh ibn Ziyad Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Tamim ibn Hudlam, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas`ud say about this verse, Until the messengers despaired of their people believing in them, and their people thought when the matter was delayed that they had been lied to due to the alleviation - so these two narrations are from both Ibn Mas`ud and Ibn Abbas, and Aisha denied that to those who interpreted it in that way, and Ibn Jarir supported her, and he addressed the well-known view of the majority and refuted the other view completely, and rejected it and refused it and did not accept it or approve of it, and God knows best.
12:111: God Almighty says: Indeed, in the report of the messengers with their people, and how We saved the believers and destroyed the disbelievers, is a lesson for those of understanding, meaning the intellects, It is not a forged statement, meaning this Qur’an could not have been forged by anyone other than God, meaning it could be lied to or fabricated, but a confirmation of what was before it, meaning: of the books sent down from the heavens, and it confirms what is correct in them, and denies what has occurred in them of distortion, alteration, and change, and rules on them as abrogated or confirmed, and a detailed account of everything, of what is permissible and forbidden, what is beloved and disliked, and other than that of commanding obedience, obligations, and recommended actions, and forbidding what is forbidden and what is similar to it of disliked things, and informing about clear matters, and about the future unseen, both general and detailed, and informing about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, and about the names and attributes, and His transcendence from resembling the creations, so for this reason it was guidance and mercy for a people who believe, by which their hearts are guided from error to right guidance, and from misguidance. To the payment, and they seek mercy from the Lord of the servants, in this worldly life and on the Day of Resurrection, so we ask God Almighty to make us among them in this world and the Hereafter, on the day when those whose faces are white and radiant will win the profit, and those whose faces are blackened by the losing deal will return. The last interpretation of Surat Yusuf, peace be upon him, and praise and thanks be to God, and with Him is help sought.
